Two days ago he vomited once; TODAY THREE OR FOUR TIMES, YELLOWISH LIKE MILK, NOT FORCEFUL. He's hot to touch BUT YOU HAVE NO THERMOMETER. PARACETAMOL HELPS FOR A FEW HOURS. HE HAS CRIED AT EVERY NAPPY CHANGE SINCE YESTERDAY AND HIS WEE SMELLS STRONG — ONLY SAY THIS IF ASKED DIRECTLY ABOUT NAPPY CHANGES OR URINE. No diarrhoea, bowels open this morning, passing wind, no bloating, NO GROIN LUMP, no screaming fits, no cold, cough, drooling or ear-pulling, no rash. SLEEPIER THAN USUAL AND DRINKING A LITTLE LESS; TWO FEWER WET NAPPIES, DARKER. No falls; home is fine; immunisations up to date; the nurse is happy with his weight. YOUR COUSIN'S CHILD HAD A COLD LAST WEEK.

REGISTER: anxious, tired; YOU SETTLE ONCE THE DOCTOR EXPLAINS A PLAN. back.dx: OESOPHAGEAL ATRESIA WITH A TRACHEO-OESOPHAGEAL FISTULA. EXPLAIN THE FILM BY DESCRIBING BEFORE NAMING: 'three colours: WHITE IS BONE — her ribs and spine; GREY IS SOFT TISSUE — her heart is this shadow; BLACK IS AIR, in her lungs. You saw us pass a thin tube through her nose. IT WAS SUPPOSED TO GO DOWN HER FOOD PIPE INTO HER STOMACH. ON THE X-RAY IT HASN'T GONE THROUGH — IT HAS CURLED UP AT THE TOP OF HER CHEST. That tells me HER FOOD PIPE HASN'T FORMED PROPERLY: IT COMES TO A BLIND END, so nothing she swallows can get down, AND IT SPILLS INTO HER WINDPIPE — which is why she splutters and goes dusky. AND THERE IS AIR IN HER TUMMY HERE; THE ONLY WAY IT CAN GET THERE IS THROUGH A SMALL CONNECTION BETWEEN HER WINDPIPE AND THE LOWER FOOD PIPE.' To the examiner, the same finding is 'COILED IN THE UPPER POUCH AT T2-T4 WITH GAS BELOW THE DIAPHRAGM'. THEN NAME IT WITH FOUR REASONS: 'OESOPHAGEAL ATRESIA — THE FOOD PIPE HASN'T JOINED UP — and in most babies it comes with a connection to the windpipe, which THE AIR IN HER TUMMY tells me she has. I think this because SHE'S BEEN FROTHY AND CHOKING WITH FEEDS SINCE BIRTH, SHE WENT DUSKY WITH A FEED, YOU HAD TOO MUCH FLUID AND A SMALL STOMACH ON THE SCANS, AND THE TUBE COULDN'T PASS.' AND LINK THE POLYHYDRAMNIOS ALOUD WHEN SHE GIVES IT: 'IF THE FOOD PIPE IS BLOCKED THE BABY CAN'T SWALLOW THE FLUID, SO IT BUILDS UP, AND THE STOMACH STAYS SMALL.' DIFFERENTIALS, EACH DISMISSED: A LARYNGEAL CLEFT letting milk into the windpipe — but THE TUBE WOULD HAVE PASSED; CHOANAL ATRESIA — but THE TUBE WENT THROUGH HER NOSE; A HEART PROBLEM, which can go with this — no murmur, BUT SHE WILL HAVE A HEART SCAN; ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA, which she may already have; and SEPSIS — the swab was negative and she is alert. A BLOCKAGE LOWER IN THE BOWEL WOULD GIVE GREEN VOMITING, AND HERS ISN'T. MANAGEMENT, AND THE FOUR SPECIFICS ARE THE MARK: NO FEEDS, so nothing more goes into her lungs; A SPECIAL SUCTION TUBE — A REPLOGLE — SITTING IN THE TOP OF THE FOOD PIPE ON CONTINUOUS LOW SUCTION TO KEEP THE SALIVA CLEARED; NURSE HER HEAD UP AT 30 TO 45 DEGREES; AND THE CHILDREN'S SURGEONS. Plus A DRIP for fluids and sugar; ANTIBIOTICS for the milk already in her lungs; AND THE ASSOCIATED-ANOMALY SCREEN — A HEART SCAN, A KIDNEY SCAN AND SPINE X-RAYS, 'BECAUSE THESE CAN GO TOGETHER'. Transfer to the Women's and Children's with the retrieval team, THE MOTHER GOING WITH HER, AND 'MOST BABIES DO VERY WELL'. If pushed, ADD 'NO BAG-MASK OR CPAP IF WE CAN AVOID IT', because it inflates the stomach through the fistula. AND ANSWER HER TWO QUESTIONS: 'IT'S NOT YOUR MILK — THIS FORMED IN THE FIRST WEEKS OF PREGNANCY' and 'YOU DIDN'T DO ANYTHING'. VERSION B — A GASLESS ABDOMEN: 'a gasless abdomen with a coiled tube means THERE IS NO CONNECTION BETWEEN THE AIRWAY AND THE LOWER OESOPHAGUS — A PURE OESOPHAGEAL ATRESIA, TYPE A. That usually means A LONG GAP between the two ends, so the surgeons MAY NOT BE ABLE TO JOIN THEM STRAIGHT AWAY: she'd have A FEEDING TUBE PLACED DIRECTLY INTO THE STOMACH AND A STAGED REPAIR over weeks to months, with the suction tube and head-up nursing continuing meanwhile. THE IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT IS OTHERWISE THE SAME.' VERSION C — THE ASSOCIATIONS VIVA: 'THE VACTERL ASSOCIATION — VERTEBRAL anomalies on a spine film, ANORECTAL malformation on inspection, CARDIAC defects AND THE SIDE OF THE AORTIC ARCH on echocardiogram, RENAL anomalies on ultrasound, and RADIAL OR LIMB anomalies on examination; plus a chromosomal check if she's dysmorphic. AROUND HALF OF THESE BABIES HAVE AT LEAST ONE, AND THE ECHO CHANGES THE OPERATIVE SIDE' — say ECHO BEFORE THEATRE and RIGHT-SIDED ARCH, which are the two details examiners reward.

back.dx: DUODENAL ATRESIA. EXPLAIN THE FILM FIRST, POINTING AT BOTH CIRCLES AND WITHOUT SAYING 'ATRESIA' YET: 'three colours: WHITE IS BONE — the spine; GREY IS SOFT TISSUE; BLACK IS AIR, WHICH IS WHAT MATTERS. What I can see is TWO BLACK CIRCLES — HERE, AND HERE. That's AIR TRAPPED IN THE STOMACH AND IN THE VERY FIRST PART OF THE BOWEL. We call it THE DOUBLE BUBBLE SIGN, and it is a sign of A BLOCKAGE IN THE FIRST PART OF THE SMALL BOWEL, THE DUODENUM. THERE'S NO AIR BEYOND IT, SO THE BLOCK IS COMPLETE.' THEN NAME IT: 'DUODENAL ATRESIA — the duodenum HASN'T FORMED PROPERLY BEFORE BIRTH, so there's a narrowing and a block, and nothing can get past it.' FOUR REASONS: 'HE'S BEEN VOMITING SINCE HIS FIRST DAY AND THE VOMIT IS GREEN — BILE — WHICH MEANS THE BLOCK IS BELOW THE STOMACH; HIS TUMMY IS FLAT, NOT SWOLLEN, WHICH FITS A BLOCK HIGH UP; YOU HAD EXTRA FLUID IN THE PREGNANCY, WHICH HAPPENS WHEN THE BABY CAN'T SWALLOW THE FLUID BECAUSE THE BOWEL IS BLOCKED; AND THE X-RAY SHOWS THE TWO BUBBLES.' THE DIFFERENTIALS, WITH VOLVULUS NAMED FIRST AS THE ONE THAT CANNOT WAIT: 'A TWIST OF THE BOWEL — THAT'S THE ONE WE MUST RULE OUT QUICKLY, BECAUSE IT CAN CUT OFF THE BLOOD SUPPLY; a block further down the small bowel; HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE, where the nerves at the end of the bowel are missing; MECONIUM ILEUS — very thick first stool blocking the bowel, WHICH CAN BE A SIGN OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS; AN IMPERFORATE ANUS — I'VE CHECKED AND HIS IS NORMAL; OESOPHAGEAL ATRESIA — but he isn't drooling or choking; SEPSIS, though your swab was negative and he's alert; and INTRACRANIAL BLEEDING from the birth, unlikely after a normal delivery.' THEN ANSWER HER THREE QUESTIONS HONESTLY: 'SOME BABIES WITH THIS BLOCKAGE DO HAVE DOWN SYNDROME — I haven't seen any signs, and THE SURGICAL TEAM WILL CHECK HIS HEART AND DO A CHROMOSOME TEST TO BE SURE.' 'NOTHING YOU DID CAUSED IT; IT HAPPENS IN THE FIRST WEEKS OF THE PREGNANCY.' 'YES — THIS IS FIXED WITH AN OPERATION, AND BABIES DO VERY WELL AFTER IT.' MANAGEMENT, IN ORDER: STOP THE FEEDS; A NASOGASTRIC TUBE to let out the air and fluid, WHICH STOPS THE VOMITING; A DRIP for fluids and sugar; BLOODS — SALTS AND A BLOOD GAS; AND THE SURGICAL TEAM NOW. Add, if there is time, that THE SURGEONS WILL CHECK HIS HEART AND, IF NEEDED, DO A DYE TEST TO MAKE SURE THERE'S NO TWIST. In a country hospital, transfer to the Women's and Children's with the mother going too. SAFETY-NET: tell the nurse straight away if he becomes FLOPPY, COLD, OR HIS TUMMY SWELLS OR LOOKS SORE. VARIANT — DISTAL GAS BEYOND THE BUBBLES: 'YES, THAT CHANGES THINGS. GAS BEYOND THE DUODENUM MEANS THE OBSTRUCTION IS INCOMPLETE — A DUODENAL STENOSIS OR WEB — OR THAT THIS IS MALROTATION WITH VOLVULUS, WHICH IS A SURGICAL EMERGENCY. I'd ask for AN URGENT UPPER GI CONTRAST STUDY to look for the position of the DUODENO-JEJUNAL FLEXURE AND A CORKSCREW SIGN, and I'd speak to the paediatric surgeon IMMEDIATELY rather than waiting for a planned repair.' DOUBLE BUBBLE DOES NOT EQUAL ATRESIA IF THERE IS DISTAL GAS — SAY THE WORD VOLVULUS. VARIANT — THE SIBLING WITH HIRSCHSPRUNG: 'that's very important — HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE CAN RUN IN FAMILIES, so I'll make sure the surgical team knows. In Hirschsprung THE TUMMY IS USUALLY SWOLLEN AND THE FIRST BOWEL MOTION IS LATE — has he passed meconium? Whichever it turns out to be, THE FIRST STEPS ARE THE SAME: no feeds, a tube, a drip, and the surgeons.' DO NOT CHANGE THE DIAGNOSIS TO MATCH THE SIBLING — ADD IT TO THE DIFFERENTIAL AND LET THE FILM DECIDE.

DID YOU HAVE THE SWAB TEST AT 36 WEEKS — FROM THE VAGINA AND BACK PASSAGE — AND WHAT WAS THE RESULT?' (TRAVEL, CONTACTS AND RUNNY NOSE ARE THE WRONG QUESTIONS HERE — THE INFECTION COMES FROM THE MOTHER.)

NEURO, DELIVERY AND THE ANTENATAL MARK: 'any swelling or redness on his head? Was the delivery long or complicated — FORCEPS OR A VACUUM CUP? Any high blood pressure or sugar problems? Medicines, alcohol, drugs, smoking? ON YOUR SCANS, WERE YOU EVER TOLD THERE WAS TOO MUCH FLUID AROUND THE BABY?' → 'YES — AT THE 32-WEEK SCAN.' → LINK IT ALOUD: 'BABIES WHO CAN'T SWALLOW THE FLUID BECAUSE THE BOWEL IS BLOCKED CAUSE EXTRA FLUID.' Then heel prick and FAMILY HISTORY OF NEWBORN VOMITING OR A BOWEL OPERATION. Then: 'is there anything you're particularly worried about?' → 'IS IT MY MILK? SHOULD I KEEP FEEDING HIM?' → 'PLEASE STOP FEEDING HIM FOR NOW — I'LL EXPLAIN WHY. IT'S NOT YOUR MILK.'

THE EXAMINATION: 'general appearance — alert, dehydration, rash, jaundice? Chest? ABDOMEN — DISTENDED OR SUNKEN, visible loops or mass? On palpation — mass, tenderness? Bowel sounds? Groin? IS THE ANUS PATENT? Scalp swelling, fontanelle? ANY FEATURES OF DOWN SYNDROME, ANY MURMUR?' → SCAPHOID abdomen, anus patent, no dysmorphism, no murmur — and the X-ray is handed over.
THE X-RAY — POINT TO BOTH CIRCLES, SAY 'DOUBLE BUBBLE' ONCE, AND DO NOT SAY ATRESIA YET (see dx).

NAME IT WITH FOUR REASONS, THEN THE DIFFERENTIALS WITH VOLVULUS FIRST (see dx) → 'DID I DO SOMETHING?' → no, this happens in the first weeks of pregnancy. → 'DOES HE HAVE DOWN SYNDROME?' → some babies with this blockage do; no signs seen, and the team will check his heart and do a chromosome test.

MANAGEMENT IN ORDER AND THE SAFETY-NET (see dx): STOP FEEDS, NASOGASTRIC TUBE, DRIP, BLOODS, SURGEONS — then transfer with the mother, and 'if he becomes floppy, cold, or his tummy swells or looks sore, tell the nurse straight away.' Then summarise.

back.dx: NEONATAL LOW BOWEL OBSTRUCTION — SAY 'OBSTRUCTION', THEN LIST THE CAUSES. THE X-RAY, EXPLAINED WITHOUT NAMING A CAUSE: 'three colours: WHITE IS BONE, GREY IS SOFT TISSUE, BLACK IS AIR — the important one. I can see MANY BLACK BUBBLES ALL OVER HIS TUMMY. EACH IS A LOOP OF BOWEL THAT HAS FILLED WITH AIR BECAUSE IT IS STRETCHED AND BLOCKED. WHEN THE BLOCK IS LOW DOWN, ALL THE LOOPS ABOVE IT SWELL LIKE THIS. So the X-ray tells me HIS BOWEL IS OBSTRUCTED — BUT NOT EXACTLY WHAT'S CAUSING IT.' For the examiner's mark, the same finding is 'MULTIPLE DILATED LOOPS WITH A SOAP-BUBBLE PATTERN ON THE RIGHT'. THE DIAGNOSIS WITH FOUR REASONS: 'he has A BLOCKAGE LOW IN THE BOWEL. I think this because HE'S VOMITING GREEN, WHICH IS BILE FROM BELOW THE STOMACH; HE HASN'T PASSED HIS FIRST STOOL OR WIND; HIS TUMMY IS SWOLLEN WITH LOOPS I CAN FEEL; AND THE X-RAY SHOWS THE SWOLLEN LOOPS.' THEN THE FIVE CAUSES, IN PLAIN WORDS — THIS IS THE LIST THE STATION IS BUILT ON: 'ONE: THE FIRST STOOL — THE MECONIUM — IS SO THICK AND STICKY IT BLOCKS THE BOWEL; THAT CAN BE A SIGN OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS, WHICH WE TEST FOR. TWO: THE NERVES THAT MAKE THE LAST PART OF THE BOWEL MOVE ARE MISSING — THAT'S HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE, THE CONDITION HIS BROTHER HAD, AND IT CAN RUN IN FAMILIES. THREE: THE BOWEL DIDN'T SETTLE IN THE RIGHT POSITION BEFORE BIRTH AND HAS TWISTED — THAT'S THE ONE WE MOVE FASTEST FOR. FOUR: THE BACK PASSAGE HASN'T FORMED — I'VE CHECKED, AND HIS IS NORMAL. FIVE: PART OF THE BOWEL DIDN'T FORM PROPERLY. THE SURGEONS AND A DYE TEST FROM THE BACK PASSAGE WILL SORT OUT WHICH.' WHEN SHE ASKS WHETHER IT IS HIRSCHSPRUNG LIKE HIS BROTHER, BE HONEST RATHER THAN DEFINITE: 'IT MAY WELL BE, GIVEN HIS BROTHER — BUT I DON'T WANT TO GUESS WHEN A TEST CAN TELL US. Most of these need an operation; some, LIKE THE STICKY STOOL, CAN SOMETIMES BE CLEARED WITH THE DYE TEST ITSELF.' MANAGEMENT, IN ORDER: STOP THE FEEDS; A NASOGASTRIC TUBE TO LET OUT THE AIR AND FLUID, WHICH STOPS THE VOMITING; A DRIP for fluids and sugar; BLOODS — SALTS, A BLOOD GAS AND AN INFECTION SCREEN, WITH ANTIBIOTICS IF THERE IS ANY CONCERN; THE CHILDREN'S SURGEONS NOW; AND TRANSFER to the Women's and Children's BY THE RETRIEVAL TEAM, WITH THE MOTHER GOING TOO. SAFETY-NET: tell the nurse immediately if HIS TUMMY BECOMES SORE OR DISCOLOURED, OR HE BECOMES FLOPPY OR COLD. VERSION B — THE NURSE: work from the charts, and her three specific questions are HAS HE BEEN EXAMINED SINCE THE VOMITING STARTED, WAS THE ANUS SPECIFICALLY SEEN TO BE PATENT, AND DOES HE LOOK DEHYDRATED — fontanelle, mouth, skin, weight against birth weight, nappies. Also ask what the MOTHER'S NOTES say: GBS swab, fever in labour, labour length, delivery, instruments, Apgars and liquor. AND GIVE INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE YOU HANG UP — MANAGEMENT INSIDE THE HISTORY IS A MARK: 'PLEASE STOP FEEDS NOW, KEEP HIM WARM, AND BRING MUM WHEN SHE WAKES — I NEED TO ASK HER ABOUT THE PREGNANCY AND FAMILY. I'M COMING TO EXAMINE HIM AND PASS AN NG TUBE, AND I'LL ORDER AN ABDOMINAL X-RAY.' Then the same content in professional register: 'multiple dilated loops — low obstruction — causes are MECONIUM ILEUS, HIRSCHSPRUNG, ATRESIA, IMPERFORATE ANUS (EXCLUDED) AND MALROTATION WITH VOLVULUS — nil by mouth, NG, IV fluids, bloods, surgeon, transfer.' VARIANT — THE TENDER ABDOMEN: 'that changes the urgency: A TENDER, DISCOLOURED ABDOMEN WITH BILIOUS VOMITING MEANS ISCHAEMIC BOWEL OR PERFORATION — most likely VOLVULUS OR A COMPLICATED MECONIUM ILEUS. I'd START IV ANTIBIOTICS NOW, resuscitate, and ask the surgeon to see him IMMEDIATELY FOR THEATRE RATHER THAN WAITING FOR A CONTRAST STUDY.' TENDERNESS MOVES THE SURGEON FROM 'NEXT' TO 'NOW' AND REMOVES THE ENEMA.

back.dx: DISTAL INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION SYNDROME — A BOWEL OBSTRUCTION OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS. THE X-RAY, DESCRIBED IN THREE COLOURS AND TWO FINDINGS: 'WHITE IS BONE — the spine; GREY IS SOFT TISSUE; BLACK IS AIR, WHICH IS WHAT MATTERS TODAY. The first thing I see is A COLLECTION OF STOOL AT THE END OF THE SMALL BOWEL, HERE ON THE RIGHT, AND IT HAS BLOCKED THE BOWEL. The second is AIR TRAPPED IN THE BOWEL ABOVE THE BLOCK — THESE BLACK SHADOWS WITH FLAT TOPS, WHICH WE CALL AIR-FLUID LEVELS; SEVERAL OF THEM TELLS US THE BOWEL IS BLOCKED. So overall, THE BOWEL IS OBSTRUCTED.' NEVER DESCRIBE STOOL YOU CANNOT SEE. NAME IT WITH BOTH NAMES: 'most likely Max has A BLOCKAGE OF THE BOWEL — in cystic fibrosis this kind of blockage is called DISTAL INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION SYNDROME. IT'S COMMON IN CHILDREN WITH CF: THEIR STOOL IS THICK AND STICKY, AND IT BUILDS UP AT THE END OF THE SMALL BOWEL AND BLOCKS IT.' FIVE REASONS: 'he's vomiting, but MORE IMPORTANTLY HE HASN'T PASSED A BOWEL MOTION FOR TWO DAYS AND ISN'T PASSING WIND; HE HAS CYSTIC FIBROSIS AND HAD A BLOCKAGE AS A NEWBORN, WHICH MAKES THIS MORE LIKELY; YOU'VE JUST STARTED SOLIDS; his tummy was distended AND I FELT A LUMP IN THE RIGHT LOWER PART, WHICH IS THE STOOL THAT HAS COLLECTED; and THE X-RAY SHOWS THE BLOCK.' THE THREE BEST DIFFERENTIALS FIRST, THEN THE REST: 'A TRAPPED HERNIA IN THE GROIN — HIS GROIN IS NORMAL; SCAR TISSUE BANDS FROM HIS OPERATION AS A BABY, WHICH CAN ALSO BLOCK THE BOWEL — THE SURGEONS WILL KEEP THAT IN MIND; and INTUSSUSCEPTION, WHERE THE BOWEL TELESCOPES INTO ITSELF, WHICH IS A BIT MORE COMMON IN CF — but he hasn't had the screaming episodes or jelly stools. Also SIMPLE CONSTIPATION, A TWIST IN THE BOWEL, A CHEST INFECTION OR ANOTHER INFECTION making him vomit, and less likely A BUMP TO THE HEAD.' WHEN SHE ASKS WHETHER THE ENZYMES CAUSED IT, ANSWER WITHOUT A FALSE PROMISE: 'STARTING SOLIDS AND THE ENZYME CHANGE PROBABLY CONTRIBUTED, BUT IT'S A KNOWN PROBLEM IN CF, NOT SOMETHING YOU DID WRONG — we'll get the dietitian to sort the doses. MOST OF THESE SETTLE WITHOUT SURGERY.' MANAGEMENT, AND THE ORDER IS THE MARK: 'OUR JOB TODAY IS TO REOPEN THE BLOCKED BOWEL. First, NOTHING BY MOUTH, AND A TUBE FROM HIS NOSE TO HIS STOMACH to let out the air and fluid — THAT ALSO STOPS THE VOMITING. A DRIP FOR FLUIDS, because he's dry and can't drink; BLOOD TESTS for his salts and a blood gas. THEN we use MEDICINE TO SOFTEN AND WASH OUT THE STOOL — A LAXATIVE THROUGH THE TUBE, OR AN ENEMA FROM THE BACK PASSAGE, DONE IN THE X-RAY DEPARTMENT. IF THAT DOESN'T CLEAR IT, THE SURGEONS WOULD NEED TO OPEN THE BLOCKAGE IN THEATRE. I'll involve the children's surgeons AND THE CF TEAM now', plus the DIETITIAN for the enzyme doses with solids. FLUIDS AND NG BEFORE THE LAXATIVE; SURGEON AS THE ESCALATION, NOT THE OPENING LINE. SAFETY-NET: tell the nurse straight away if he VOMITS GREEN AGAIN, HIS TUMMY BECOMES PAINFUL, OR HE BECOMES DROWSY. VARIANT — THE FILM WITH NO VISIBLE STOOL: describe only what is there — 'AIR TRAPPED IN THE BOWEL, SEVERAL AIR-FLUID LEVELS, SO THE BOWEL IS BLOCKED. THE X-RAY DOESN'T SHOW ME EXACTLY WHAT IS BLOCKING IT, BUT WITH HIS CYSTIC FIBROSIS, NO STOOL AND NO WIND, AND THE LUMP I FELT ON THE RIGHT, THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE IS A BUILD-UP OF THICK STOOL.' BOWEL OBSTRUCTION AS THE DIAGNOSIS WITH DIOS AS THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE PASSES. VARIANT — THE MANAGEMENT PUSH: 'after IV rehydration and NG decompression, for AN INCOMPLETE OBSTRUCTION I'd start AN OSMOTIC WASHOUT — MACROGOL BY NASOGASTRIC TUBE, OR DILUTED ORAL GASTROGRAFIN per the CF protocol — with the CF team. For A COMPLETE OBSTRUCTION I'd ask for A GASTROGRAFIN ENEMA UNDER FLUOROSCOPY, WHICH IS DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC. I'd OPERATE — with paediatric surgery — IF THERE IS PERITONISM, BILIOUS VOMITING WITH A TENDER ABDOMEN, OR FAILURE OF TWO ATTEMPTS AT WASHOUT; the operation is DECOMPRESSION AND WASHOUT THROUGH AN ENTEROTOMY, NOT RESECTION.' NAMING THE ESCALATION CRITERIA IS THE MARK.
plan: VITALS AND HYDRATION, THEN OPEN: 'could I have the vital signs and hydration status first?' Then: 'tell me more about the vomiting.' → 'he's vomited twice since yesterday. Not huge amounts, but HE'S NOT HIMSELF AND HIS TUMMY LOOKS BIG. WITH HIS CYSTIC FIBROSIS I JUST PANIC EVERY TIME SOMETHING HAPPENS.' → 'that's understandable — EVERY NEW SYMPTOM FEELS BIGGER WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS. We'll sort it out together.'

THE LEAD POINT — FOUR QUESTIONS IN NINETY SECONDS: 'because Max has cystic fibrosis, I'd like to ask about that. WHEN WAS HE DIAGNOSED? WHAT TREATMENT IS HE ON — enzymes with feeds, antibiotics, inhalers or physio, salt, vitamins — AND IS HE GETTING ALL OF IT? HAS HE HAD ANY OPERATIONS ON HIS TUMMY? ARE YOU REGULAR WITH THE GP AND THE CF CLINIC?' → 'YES — HE HAD AN OPERATION IN THE FIRST DAYS FOR A BLOCKAGE OF THE BOWEL.' → SAY THE WORDS BACK: 'SO A LAPAROTOMY FOR MECONIUM ILEUS. THAT MATTERS.' Then recurrent chest infections and growth.

THE BOWEL BLOCK: 'WHEN DID HE LAST OPEN HIS BOWELS? IS HE PASSING WIND? Before this, any diarrhoea or blood in the stool? Any constipation in the past? IS HIS TUMMY SWOLLEN?' → two days ago, NO WIND, bigger and tight.

THE OBSTRUCTION CAUSES — AND TWO PRECIPITANTS ARE HANDED TO YOU HERE: 'any swelling or LUMP IN THE GROIN? Episodes of SCREAMING WITH HIS LEGS DRAWN UP, GOING PALE, RED-JELLY STOOL? Recent infection or vaccine? ANY PREVIOUS BLOCKAGES SINCE THE NEWBORN ONE? ANY CHANGE IN FEEDING RECENTLY — SOLIDS, FORMULA? DID HIS ENZYME DOSE CHANGE? IS HE DRINKING ENOUGH? HAS IT BEEN HOT?' → 'WE STARTED SOLIDS TWO WEEKS AGO — I'VE BEEN GUESSING THE ENZYMES WITH THE FOOD', and he's drinking less. → ACKNOWLEDGE THEM ALOUD: 'NEW SOLIDS AND DEHYDRATION ARE BOTH IMPORTANT HERE.'

REFLUX, INFECTION, WELL-BABY, NEURO AND BIRTH: refuses feeds or arches; fever, sick contacts, travel, IS THE COUGH WORSE THAN USUAL, nappy-change crying; alert or drowsy, drinking, WET NAPPIES; falls or head knocks; DID HE HAVE TROUBLE PASSING HIS FIRST BOWEL MOTION, heel prick, immunisations, and what he is fed. Then: 'anything you're particularly worried about?' → 'IS THE CF BLOCKING HIS BOWEL AGAIN? WILL HE NEED ANOTHER OPERATION?'

THE EXAMINATION, WITH THE MASS ASKED FOR BY NAME: 'general appearance — alert or drowsy, dehydration, rash? Throat and ears? Chest — air entry, added sounds? ABDOMEN ON INSPECTION — DISTENSION, SCARS, VISIBLE PERISTALSIS OR MASS? ON PALPATION — ANY MASS, AND WHERE? TENDERNESS, GUARDING, RIGIDITY? BOWEL SOUNDS? Groin and scrotum? Urine dipstick?' → the right lower quadrant mass, HIGH-PITCHED BOWEL SOUNDS, and the X-ray.
THE X-RAY IN THREE COLOURS AND TWO FINDINGS (see dx) — the stool collection on the right, then the air-fluid levels, then the conclusion.

NAME IT WITH BOTH NAMES AND FIVE REASONS, THEN THE THREE BEST DIFFERENTIALS AND THE REST (see dx) → 'IS IT BECAUSE I GOT THE ENZYMES WRONG WITH THE SOLIDS?' → contributed, but a known problem of CF, and the dietitian will sort the doses.

MANAGEMENT IN ORDER AND THE SAFETY-NET (see dx): nil by mouth and NG, fluids and bloods, THEN the laxative or enema, THEN the surgeons as escalation — plus the CF team and the dietitian. → 'WILL HE NEED ANOTHER OPERATION?' → 'MOST OF THESE SETTLE WITHOUT SURGERY.' Then summarise.

back.dx: A SINGLE UNPROVOKED SEIZURE — NOT EPILEPSY, AND NOT A FEBRILE CONVULSION. NAME IT AND DEFINE IT: 'Ethan has had what we call AN UNPROVOKED SEIZURE. A SEIZURE IS A SUDDEN BURST OF ABNORMAL ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY IN THE BRAIN. THE JERKING OF ALL FOUR LIMBS, THE EYES ROLLING BACK, WETTING HIMSELF AND BEING CONFUSED AFTERWARDS ARE ALL TYPICAL OF A SEIZURE.' THEN THE REASONS — AND THE REASONS ARE THE EXCLUDED CAUSES, SAID ONE BY ONE IN PLAIN WORDS: 'WHEN A CHILD HAS A SEIZURE WE ALWAYS LOOK FOR A REASON. HE HASN'T HAD A HEAD INJURY. HE HASN'T HAD A FEVER, SO I'M NOT WORRIED ABOUT AN INFECTION OF THE BRAIN LIKE MENINGITIS. HE'D EATEN, SO A LOW SUGAR IS UNLIKELY — AND HIS SUGAR HERE IS NORMAL. HE'S NOT ON ANY MEDICINES. HE HASN'T HAD THE LONG-STANDING HEADACHES OR MORNING VOMITING THAT WOULD MAKE ME THINK OF A GROWTH IN THE BRAIN. AND THERE'S NOTHING TO SUGGEST STRESS IS BEHIND IT. WHEN WE LOOK AND FIND NOTHING, WE CALL IT UNPROVOKED.' THEN HER THREE QUESTIONS, ANSWERED IN ORDER: 'THE FITS HE HAD AS A BABY WERE WITH FEVERS, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT THING AND VERY COMMON; TODAY THERE WAS NO FEVER. EPILEPSY MEANS REPEATED UNPROVOKED SEIZURES, AND ETHAN HAS HAD ONE. HIS DAD'S SINGLE SEIZURE IS WORTH KNOWING BUT DOESN'T MEAN ETHAN HAS EPILEPSY. MOST CHILDREN WHO HAVE ONE SEIZURE DON'T GO ON TO HAVE EPILEPSY, THOUGH SOME DO HAVE ANOTHER — THAT'S WHY HE'LL BE SEEN BY THE CHILDREN'S SPECIALISTS. AND NO — NOTHING YOU DID CAUSED THIS.' DIFFERENTIALS, BRIEFLY: 'I've also considered other things that CAN LOOK LIKE A FIT — A FAINT, A HEART RHYTHM PROBLEM, A STRESS-RELATED EPISODE, A SEVERE MIGRAINE — and none of them fit what happened today.' THEN STAY INSIDE THE TASK: 'I'M NOT GOING TO GO INTO TESTS TODAY; THE SPECIALISTS WILL DECIDE ABOUT THOSE. What's your biggest worry?' → 'THAT IT'LL HAPPEN AT SCHOOL AGAIN AND NO ONE WILL KNOW WHAT TO DO' → THE WRITTEN PLAN: 'STAY CALM, NOTHING IN HIS MOUTH, PROTECT HIM FROM INJURY, DON'T HOLD HIM DOWN, ROLL HIM ON HIS SIDE WHEN IT STOPS, AND CALL 000 IF IT LASTS MORE THAN FIVE MINUTES OR HE DOESN'T WAKE UP.' VARIANT B — THE 15-YEAR-OLD ACCUSED OF SHOPLIFTING: ask whether HER EYES WERE OPEN OR CLOSED, whether she WET HERSELF, and WHETHER SHE REMEMBERS ALL OF IT. Then: 'WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU WAS REAL AND FRIGHTENING, AND YOU DIDN'T FAKE IT. Because you COULD HEAR EVERYTHING, YOUR EYES WERE CLOSED, YOU WERE BREATHING VERY FAST BEFOREHAND AND IT CAME ON AT A MOMENT OF INTENSE STRESS, I think this was your body's response to overwhelming stress rather than an electrical seizure. IT'S CALLED A NON-EPILEPTIC SEIZURE. It's treatable, and IT DOESN'T NEED EPILEPSY MEDICINES.' Then the safety and mood screen, INCLUDING THOUGHTS OF SELF-HARM. NEVER SAY 'FAKE' OR 'PSEUDO'; never dismiss the shoplifting accusation, which is the stressor; AND DO NOT MAKE THE REVERSE ERROR of calling a genuine seizure psychogenic because a teenager was upset — AN ECG AND A PROPER HISTORY STILL APPLY. VARIANT C — RIGHT ARM ONLY, SEVEN MINUTES, THREE WEEKS OF MORNING VOMITING: 'THREE THINGS CONCERN ME: THE JERKING WAS ON ONE SIDE ONLY, IT WENT ON FOR SEVEN MINUTES, AND HE HAS BEEN VOMITING IN THE MORNINGS WITH HEADACHES FOR WEEKS. Together those make me want to LOOK AT HIS BRAIN TODAY RATHER THAN WAIT — a scan, and the children's neurologist. These are the signs WE NEVER LEAVE FOR LATER.' Examine the fundi and gait. 'Unprovoked seizure, first seizure clinic in six weeks' is the fail here. VARIANT D — THE 12-MONTH-OLD WITH A FEBRILE CONVULSION: 'a SIMPLE FEBRILE CONVULSION. I call it simple because ALL FOUR LIMBS WERE INVOLVED, IT LASTED UNDER FIFTEEN MINUTES, IT ONLY HAPPENED ONCE, AND SHE WOKE UP STRAIGHT AWAY — and because she has NO HISTORY OF FITS WITHOUT FEVER AND NO DEVELOPMENTAL PROBLEMS. I've also checked the things that matter: NO RASH, NO VOMITING, SHE'S ALERT, WET NAPPIES NORMAL — so I'm not worried about meningitis. BECAUSE IT'S SIMPLE, SHE NEEDS NO TESTS TODAY — NO SCAN, NO BLOOD TEST.' Find and treat the source of the fever, paracetamol for comfort, fluids. 'IT CAN HAPPEN AGAIN WITH ANOTHER FEVER, AND PARACETAMOL DOESN'T PREVENT THAT, BUT MOST CHILDREN GROW OUT OF IT AND IT IS NOT EPILEPSY.' Then the same first-aid plan. The traps there are saying 'febrile convulsion' WITHOUT FIRST RULING OUT THE SOURCE, ordering an EEG, and PROMISING IT WILL NOT RECUR.
plan: VITALS AND A BEDSIDE GLUCOSE, THEN THE CONCERN AND THE NOTE: 'may I have his vital signs AND A BEDSIDE GLUCOSE?' Then: 'Ethan is being watched by our nurses. How can I help you today?' → 'the school rang — he had a fit in class. I'M SO WORRIED. HERE, THE TEACHER WROTE IT ALL DOWN. IS IT EPILEPSY? HIS DAD HAD ONE.' → 'I'm sorry — THAT'S A FRIGHTENING CALL TO GET. He's in safe hands. Thank you for the note; let me read it... THAT'S VERY HELPFUL. A FEW THINGS AREN'T ON IT, SO I'LL ASK YOU THOSE.'

THE GAPS IN THE NOTE: 'it says his arms and legs were jerking — DID THE TEACHER SAY WHETHER IT WAS ALL FOUR LIMBS, OR JUST ONE SIDE? DID HE BITE HIS TONGUE? ANY FROTHING? WAS HE BLUE OR BREATHING STRANGELY? HAS ANYTHING LIKE THIS HAPPENED BEFORE — INCLUDING STARING SPELLS OR BLANKING OUT?' → all four limbs, no tongue bite, pale not blue — AND 'HE HAD FITS WITH FEVERS WHEN HE WAS A BABY.' → 'DID HE HAVE A FEVER TODAY OR THIS WEEK?' → NO. → record it and KEEP GOING.

THE FOUR BEFORE-QUESTIONS — THE SCORED BLOCK: 'WHAT WAS HE DOING JUST BEFORE IT HAPPENED? The note says he felt sick — DID HE SAY ANYTHING ELSE, A FUNNY FEELING, A SMELL, DIZZINESS? ANY HEAD INJURY OR FALL RECENTLY? HAD HE MISSED ANY MEALS — DID HE HAVE BREAKFAST?' Then: 'any fever or rash in the last few days? Is he on any medicines — COULD HE HAVE GOT INTO ANYTHING AT HOME? Sleeping badly? Any stress? A lot of screens or flashing lights?'

AFTER: 'when he woke, WAS HE CONFUSED AND DROWSY — HOW LONG FOR? DID HE WAKE STRAIGHT AWAY OR GRADUALLY? DOES HE REMEMBER IT? ANY WEAKNESS ON ONE SIDE AFTERWARDS?' → fifteen minutes, gradual, no memory, no weakness.

THE SCREENS, WHICH BELONG HERE AND NOT EARLIER: neurological — headaches, blurred vision, weakness, numbness, speech; CARDIAC — chest pain, racing heart, breathlessness; gastrointestinal; THE TUMOUR QUESTIONS — LONG-STANDING HEADACHES, VOMITING IN THE MORNINGS, WEIGHT LOSS; then home, who lives there, stress, school and bullying, AND 'WAS HE BREATHING FAST BEFORE IT STARTED?' (Running the symptom screens BEFORE the four before-questions is the ordering trap — the checklist is INCIDENT, BEFORE, AFTER, THEN SCREENS.)

BACKGROUND: 'any concerns about his development? Any other medical problems? Immunisations up to date? ANY FAMILY HISTORY OF SEIZURES OR EPILEPSY — YOU MENTIONED HIS DAD? ANYONE WHO DIED SUDDENLY YOUNG, OR DROWNED?' → the father's single seizure at 19 after heavy drinking, never repeated.
NAME IT AND DEFINE IT, THEN GIVE THE EXCLUDED CAUSES ONE BY ONE AS THE REASONS (see dx). (A diagnosis with no reasons fails — AND SO DOES 'IT'S EPILEPSY' OR 'IT'S JUST A FEBRILE FIT'.)

HER THREE QUESTIONS, THE BRIEF DIFFERENTIALS, AND STAYING INSIDE THE TASK (see dx) → 'BUT HE HAD FITS AS A BABY, AND HIS DAD HAD ONE — IS IT EPILEPSY?' → the febrile fits were different, EPILEPSY MEANS REPEATED UNPROVOKED SEIZURES AND HE HAS HAD ONE. Then: 'WHAT'S YOUR BIGGEST WORRY?' → the school → the written first-aid plan, and a summary.

pefe: Role-player: AMANDA, 36, Ethan's mother, works at the council office; married to Dave, a fitter at the port; daughter Mia, 4. ETHAN is a healthy, happy Year 2 boy — NO medications or allergies, immunised, NORMAL DEVELOPMENT, doing well at school, no bullying, sleeps well. HE HAD TWO BRIEF FEBRILE CONVULSIONS AS A BABY at 6 and 12 months, both simple. DAVE HAD ONE SEIZURE AT 19 AFTER A NIGHT OF HEAVY DRINKING — investigated, no treatment, never recurred. NO SUDDEN DEATHS IN THE FAMILY.

YOU HAVE THE TEACHER'S NOTE — read it out or hand it over when asked about the event. From the teacher you know: ALL FOUR LIMBS JERKED, EYES ROLLED BACK, ABOUT A MINUTE, WET HIMSELF, PALE NOT BLUE, NO TONGUE BITE SEEN, SLEEPY AND CONFUSED FOR FIFTEEN MINUTES then normal. HE SAID 'I FEEL SICK' JUST BEFORE. He had WEET-BIX for breakfast, NO fever or illness this week, NO head injury, nothing in the house he could have taken. MILD HEADACHE AFTERWARDS, now gone. No vomiting, no chest symptoms, NO MORNING VOMITING, no weight loss, no weakness.

REGISTER: anxious, controlled, factual. YOUR HIDDEN QUESTION IS 'IS IT EPILEPSY LIKE HIS DAD?' — RAISE IT ONCE WHEN ASKED ABOUT FAMILY HISTORY, AND AGAIN IF THE DOCTOR NAMES THE DIAGNOSIS WITHOUT EXPLAINING. IF NEVER ASKED ABOUT CONCERNS, VOLUNTEER AT MINUTE FIVE: 'WHAT IF IT HAPPENS AT SCHOOL AGAIN?' Score them on: vitals and glucose; concern addressed; USES THE NOTE AND ASKS WHAT IS MISSING; all four limbs versus one side; tongue, frothing, incontinence; previous events; FEVER TODAY; activity before; WARNING; HEAD INJURY; MISSED MEALS; fever and rash; medications and ingestion; sleep, stress and lights; POST-ICTAL CONFUSION; memory; the neurological screen; the cardiac screen; the gastrointestinal screen; THE TUMOUR QUESTIONS; home, school and hyperventilation; development; FAMILY HISTORY INCLUDING SUDDEN DEATH; SAYS 'UNPROVOKED SEIZURE'; DEFINES SEIZURE; THE REASONS ARE THE CAUSES EXCLUDED ONE BY ONE; handles 'febrile' and 'epilepsy' correctly; offers differentials; STAYS WITHIN THE TASK with no investigation lecture; and invites questions. AUTOMATIC FAIL: NO CAUSES-OF-SEIZURE QUESTIONS; LABELS IT EPILEPSY OR FEBRILE CONVULSION.
fails: ★ Labelling it epilepsy, or labelling it a febrile convulsion — both are automatic fails
★ Asking no causes-of-seizure questions at all, or naming the diagnosis with no reasons when the reasons ARE the excluded causes
Being pulled to febrile convulsion by the infant fits — ask about fever today, record the old fits, and keep going, because age 7 and afebrile is not a febrile convulsion
Running the symptom screens before the four before-questions — the checklist is incident, then before, then after, then screens

Not asking what is missing from the teacher's note; skipping the tumour questions or the sudden-death family history; and drifting into investigations and management when the task explicitly excludes them

back.dx: COMPLETE KAWASAKI DISEASE. EXPLAIN IT: 'Jack most likely has a condition called KAWASAKI DISEASE. In this condition there is INFLAMMATION IN THE BLOOD TUBES — THE BLOOD VESSELS — CAUSED BY THE IMMUNE SYSTEM WORKING ABNORMALLY. IT IS NOT AN INFECTION HE CAUGHT, AND IT IS NOT SOMETHING YOU MISSED.' THEN THE REASONS — AND THE REASONS ARE THE CRITERIA, OR THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOT CREDITED: 'HIS FEVER FOR MORE THAN FIVE DAYS THAT IS NOT SETTLING WITH PARACETAMOL, THE RASH INCLUDING HIS PALMS AND FEET, HIS RED EYES, HIS CRACKED LIPS AND RED TONGUE, HIS SWOLLEN PEELING HANDS, AND THE GLANDS IN HIS NECK.' THE DIFFERENTIALS MUST BE CONDITIONS, NEVER ORGANISMS — no EBV, no streptococcus, no adenovirus: 'A THROAT INFECTION CALLED SCARLET FEVER, which can look similar; A SERIOUS BLOOD INFECTION OR MENINGITIS; MEASLES AND OTHER VIRAL RASHES; and THE USUAL INFECTIONS OF THE EARS, CHEST, TUMMY, URINE, JOINTS AND SKIN, WHICH I COULD NOT FIND ON EXAMINATION.' HER THREE QUESTIONS: 'IS IT DANGEROUS?' → 'IT IS SERIOUS MAINLY BECAUSE IT CAN AFFECT THE SMALL BLOOD VESSELS OF THE HEART, WHICH IS WHY WE TREAT IT EARLY.' 'DID THE OTHER DOCTOR MISS IT?' → 'TWO DAYS AGO IT WOULD HAVE LOOKED LIKE A VIRUS; THE SIGNS THAT MAKE IT CLEAR HAVE APPEARED SINCE' — never blame the previous doctor. 'IS IT CONTAGIOUS?' → NO. MANAGEMENT: 'Jack needs to go to hospital TODAY — the Women's and Children's. I'll RING THE PAEDIATRIC TEAM NOW and arrange transport. In hospital they will give him INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN, WHICH SETTLES THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND REDUCES THE INFLAMMATION. He will start A LOW DOSE OF ASPIRIN TO PROTECT THE BLOOD VESSELS OF THE HEART, and he will have AN ECHOCARDIOGRAM — NOW, AT TWO WEEKS AND AT SIX WEEKS — to look at THE CORONARY ARTERIES. The team will keep him on aspirin UNTIL THE SCANS ARE CLEAR. There is a small risk with aspirin DURING CHICKENPOX OR FLU, so they'll talk about the flu vaccine, and HIS NEXT LIVE VACCINES WILL BE DELAYED FOR ABOUT ELEVEN MONTHS AFTER THE IMMUNOGLOBULIN.' AND THE ASPIRIN QUESTION ANSWERED HONESTLY: 'you're right that WE AVOID ASPIRIN FOR ORDINARY FEVERS; KAWASAKI DISEASE IS ONE OF THE FEW CONDITIONS WHERE THE BENEFIT CLEARLY OUTWEIGHS THE SMALL RISK, and it is given under specialist supervision.' PATS for travel and accommodation. SAYING 'LET'S DO SOME BLOOD TESTS AND SEE' IS A FAIL — THE IVIG WINDOW IS TEN DAYS FROM FEVER ONSET AND YOU ARE ON DAY FIVE. THE VARIANTS: AN INFANT UNDER 12 MONTHS WITH SIX DAYS OF FEVER, CRP 90 AND ONLY CONJUNCTIVITIS AND RASH — 'he does not meet the full criteria, BUT BABIES UNDER ONE OFTEN SHOW FEWER FEATURES AND CARRY THE HIGHEST RISK TO THE HEART. I'M TREATING THIS AS INCOMPLETE KAWASAKI DISEASE and arranging AN ECHOCARDIOGRAM AND PAEDIATRIC REVIEW TODAY, NOT IN A WEEK.' TONSILS WITH WHITE EXUDATE — 'EXUDATE WITH A STRAWBERRY TONGUE AND A RASH MAKES SCARLET FEVER MY LEADING DIAGNOSIS. I'd confirm with A THROAT SWAB, start PHENOXYMETHYLPENICILLIN FOR TEN DAYS, and STILL REVIEW THE OTHER FEATURES CAREFULLY — IF THE FEVER PERSISTS BEYOND FIVE DAYS DESPITE PENICILLIN I WOULD RECONSIDER KAWASAKI DISEASE.'
plan: VITALS FIRST — NONE ARE GIVEN — THEN THE CONCERN WITHOUT BLAME: 'Examiner, could I have the vital signs please?' → 39.2, HR 130. Then: 'he's been burning up for five days — THE OTHER DOCTOR SAID IT'S A VIRUS BUT HE'S GETTING WORSE. I JUST WANT SOMEONE TO TAKE THIS SERIOUSLY.' → 'I can hear that, and five days of fever in a little one is frightening. WHAT YOU WERE TOLD ON MONDAY WAS REASONABLE AT THE TIME — MOST FEVERS ARE VIRAL — BUT A FEVER STILL THIS HIGH AT DAY FIVE NEEDS A FRESH LOOK, AND THAT IS WHAT WE'LL DO TOGETHER NOW.' (Do NOT comment on the previous GP — if you criticise him she pushes with 'SO HE GOT IT WRONG?')

EXPLORE THE FEVER: 'have you measured it? How high? Is it there all the time? Getting worse? WHAT HAVE YOU GIVEN HIM — AND IS IT HELPING? Any shivers?' → 39, constant, AND PARACETAMOL DOES NOTHING. → SAY IT ALOUD: 'THAT TELLS ME THIS IS MORE THAN A SIMPLE VIRUS' — then KEEP HUNTING.

THE EIGHT-GROUP SOURCE HUNT, SIGNPOSTED: 'I'M GOING TO GO THROUGH THE PLACES AN INFECTION CAN HIDE.' EARS AND THROAT — ear pain, runny nose, sore throat, DROOLING, VOICE CHANGE, NECK LUMPS, RASH. CHEST — cough, difficulty breathing, noisy breathing. TUMMY — vomiting, diarrhoea, pain. WATERWORKS — smelly urine, crying when he wees. JOINTS AND SKIN — SWOLLEN RED JOINTS, LIMPING, rash. MENINGITIS — headache, sore neck, BOTHERED BY LIGHT. THE WELL-BABY THREE — alert or drowsy, eating and drinking, WET NAPPIES. (The role-player volunteers the rash ONLY if asked — AND A CANDIDATE WHO STOPS AT 'RED THROAT' WALKS OUT WITH SCARLET FEVER AND FAILS.)

EXPLORE THE RASH WHEN SHE GIVES IT: 'where did it start? IS IT ITCHY? Does it hurt him? DOES IT FADE WHEN YOU PRESS IT? ANY PEELING?' → chest two days ago, not itchy, BLANCHING, maybe a little peeling at the fingertips.

THE KAWASAKI QUESTIONS AND CIST: 'HAVE HIS EYES BEEN RED? ARE HIS LIPS DRY OR CRACKED? ANY GLANDS OR LUMPS IN HIS NECK? ANY PEELING ON HIS PALMS OR FEET?' Then TRAVEL, SICK CONTACTS, IMMUNISATIONS. → BOTH EYES RED FOR TWO DAYS WITHOUT DISCHARGE, CRACKED BLEEDING LIPS, A LUMP ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE NECK.

THE EXAMINATION IN NINE STEPS, THEN THE FIVE KAWASAKI POINTS BY NAME: 'general appearance — alert or drowsy, DEHYDRATION, and THE RASH — SITE, COLOUR, WARM, TENDER, SURFACE? Vitals. ENT — ANY EXUDATE? Chest — air entry, added sounds. Heart — S1, S2, murmur. Abdomen. A FULL JOINT EXAMINATION. A FULL LYMPH NODE EXAMINATION — SIZE AND TENDERNESS. NECK STIFFNESS. URINE DIPSTICK. And specifically: STRAWBERRY TONGUE? CRACKED LIPS? CONJUNCTIVITIS — BILATERAL, ANY DISCHARGE? RED OR SWOLLEN HANDS AND FEET? DESQUAMATION?' (If you never say 'full joint examination', 'full lymph node examination', 'neck stiffness', or ask the Kawasaki points, THE EXAMINER WILL NOT VOLUNTEER THEM.)

THE DIAGNOSIS WITH THE CRITERIA AS THE REASONS, THEN DIFFERENTIALS AS CONDITIONS (see dx) → 'KAWASAKI? I'VE NEVER HEARD OF IT. IS IT DANGEROUS?' / 'DID THE OTHER DOCTOR MISS IT?' / 'IS IT CONTAGIOUS — MY DAUGHTER IS AT HOME.'

MANAGEMENT AND CLOSE (see dx): hospital TODAY, ring the paediatric team now, IVIG, LOW-DOSE ASPIRIN, and ECHO NOW, AT TWO WEEKS AND AT SIX WEEKS — plus the flu vaccine discussion, live vaccines delayed eleven months, PATS, and practice follow-up. → 'ASPIRIN? I THOUGHT CHILDREN CAN'T HAVE ASPIRIN.' → answer it honestly. (If you offer blood tests and review tomorrow she says 'CAN'T WE DO SOMETHING TODAY?')

pefe: Role-player: MARY, 32, Jack's mother. Jack is 4, healthy, FULLY IMMUNISED, at kindy three days a week. You work at the IGA; your partner is FIFO. JACK HAS HAD A FEVER SINCE FRIDAY — TODAY IS WEDNESDAY. You saw the GP on Monday, WHO SAID IT WAS VIRAL. You give paracetamol every four hours AND IT HARDLY HELPS. He is MISERABLE BUT AWAKE, DRINKING VERY LITTLE, TWO WET NAPPIES YESTERDAY. He has A BLOTCHY RED RASH ON HIS CHEST AND TUMMY SINCE MONDAY, RED PUFFY HANDS AND FEET, BOTH EYES RED FOR TWO DAYS WITHOUT DISCHARGE, CRACKED BLEEDING LIPS, AND A LUMP ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF HIS NECK. His throat looked red on Sunday. No cough, vomiting, diarrhoea, urinary symptoms, limp, headache or neck pain. No travel; colds at kindy.

HIDDEN AGENDA: YOU ARE ANGRY THAT MONDAY'S DOCTOR 'FOBBED YOU OFF' AND TERRIFIED SOMETHING SERIOUS HAS BEEN MISSED. REGISTER: anxious, TEARFUL WHEN THE WORD 'HEART' IS USED, relieved when the doctor is calm and specific. HOW TO PLAY IT: VOLUNTEER ONLY THE FEVER AND THE PANADOL FAILURE. MENTION THE RASH, THE EYES AND THE LIPS ONLY IF ASKED DIRECTLY. IF THE DOCTOR CRITICISES MONDAY'S GP, SAY 'SO HE GOT IT WRONG?' AND PUSH. If the doctor has not asked what worries you by minute five, say 'IS THIS SOMETHING BAD?'. IF THE DOCTOR SUGGESTS BLOOD TESTS AND REVIEW TOMORROW, SAY 'CAN'T WE DO SOMETHING TODAY?'

Score them on: ASKED VITALS FIRST; acknowledged your worry WITHOUT BLAMING THE PREVIOUS GP; asked measured, medication and whether it is helping; NAMED ALL EIGHT GROUPS — ENT, chest, GI, urine, joints and skin, meningitis, sepsis, Kawasaki; asked about the rash AND EXPLORED IT; ASKED PEELING, RED EYES, CRACKED LIPS AND NECK GLANDS; travel, contacts and immunisation; THE EXAMINATION INCLUDING FULL JOINTS, FULL NODES, NECK STIFFNESS, DIPSTICK AND EXUDATE; ASKED STRAWBERRY TONGUE, LIPS, CONJUNCTIVITIS, HANDS AND DESQUAMATION; SAID 'KAWASAKI DISEASE' WITH A ONE-LINE EXPLANATION AND LISTED THE REASONS; DIFFERENTIALS AS CONDITIONS; HOSPITAL TODAY, IVIG, ASPIRIN AND THREE ECHOES; answered the aspirin question honestly; and summarised to the examiner.
fails: ★ Stopping the source hunt at 'red throat' — the rash, eyes, lips and neck glands are volunteered only if asked, and without them you walk out with scarlet fever
★ Offering blood tests and review tomorrow — the IVIG window is ten days from fever onset and you are on day five
Not asking for the vital signs, which are deliberately withheld from the stem
Giving differentials as organisms rather than conditions, or naming the diagnosis without listing the criteria as reasons

Never saying 'full joint examination', 'full lymph node examination' or 'neck stiffness', and never asking the five Kawasaki points by name — the examiner will not volunteer any of them; and criticising the previous GP, which earns 'so he got it wrong?'

back.dx: ACUTE EPIGLOTTITIS — SUPRAGLOTTITIS — WITH IMPENDING UPPER-AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION. EXPLAIN IT SLOWLY AND IN SHORT SENTENCES: 'Oliver most likely has a condition called EPIGLOTTITIS. THE EPIGLOTTIS IS A SMALL FLAP OF TISSUE AT THE BACK OF THE THROAT THAT ACTS LIKE A LID OVER THE WINDPIPE. IT HAS BECOME INFECTED AND SWOLLEN, and that's why HE CAN'T SWALLOW, IS DRIBBLING, SOUNDS MUFFLED AND IS BREATHING NOISILY.' FIVE REASONS: 'THE HIGH FEVER THAT CAME ON OVER HOURS, THE DROOLING, THE CHANGE IN HIS VOICE, THE TROUBLE SWALLOWING, THE WAY HE'S SITTING TO KEEP HIS AIRWAY OPEN — AND BECAUSE THERE'S NO COUGH, WHICH WE'D EXPECT WITH CROUP. The fact that some of his vaccines were missed also fits, BECAUSE THE GERM THAT USUALLY CAUSES THIS IS ONE WE VACCINATE AGAINST.' THE DIFFERENTIALS: 'CROUP, which usually comes with A BARKING COUGH AND A COLD; A SWALLOWED OBJECT, which comes on suddenly in a well child; AN ABSCESS AT THE BACK OF THE THROAT; and A SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION. His picture fits epiglottitis best, and IT'S THE ONE WE TREAT AS AN EMERGENCY UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.' AND WHEN SHE ASKS WHETHER IT IS HER FAULT: 'THIS ISN'T ABOUT BLAME — RIGHT NOW IT'S ABOUT GETTING HIM SAFE, AND WE'LL SORT THE VACCINES OUT LATER.' MANAGEMENT, AND THE ORDER IS THE MARK: ONE — 'HE STAYS EXACTLY WHERE HE IS, UPRIGHT ON YOUR LAP; WE WON'T LAY HIM DOWN OR UPSET HIM, AND NOBODY WILL LOOK IN HIS MOUTH.' TWO — 'OXYGEN — I'll ask you to HOLD THE MASK NEAR HIS FACE.' THREE — 'I'M CALLING THE SENIOR DOCTOR AND THE ANAESTHETIST NOW, AND OUR RETRIEVAL SERVICE, MedSTAR KIDS, because the safest place for him is THE CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL INTENSIVE CARE WITH A TEAM THAT CAN PROTECT HIS AIRWAY. If his breathing gets worse THEY WILL PUT A TUBE INTO HIS WINDPIPE UNDER ANAESTHETIC TO KEEP IT OPEN — THAT'S A PLANNED, SAFE STEP, NOT A LAST RESORT.' FOUR — 'ONCE HIS AIRWAY IS SAFE he'll have A DRIP WITH STRONG ANTIBIOTICS INTO THE VEIN, FLUIDS because he's dry, and medicine for the fever. NOTHING TO EAT OR DRINK.' THEN HER THREE QUESTIONS: 'CAN I STAY WITH HIM?' → 'YES — YOU STAYING CALM WITH HIM IS PART OF THE TREATMENT.' 'WILL HE NEED AN OPERATION?' → 'THE TUBE ISN'T AN OPERATION; it's done by the anaesthetist and USUALLY COMES OUT IN A DAY OR TWO once the swelling settles.' 'WHAT ABOUT HIS SISTER?' → 'if tests show it's the germ we think, THE PUBLIC HEALTH UNIT WILL BE TOLD AND THE FAMILY MAY NEED A SHORT COURSE OF ANTIBIOTICS TO PROTECT HER, and we'll catch up everyone's vaccines.' THE VARIANTS. A LATERAL NECK X-RAY: 'this shows A SWOLLEN EPIGLOTTIS — THE THUMB SIGN — with THICKENED ARYEPIGLOTTIC FOLDS. It confirms epiglottitis. I WOULD NOT HAVE SENT HIM FOR THIS FILM BEFORE SECURING HIS AIRWAY; if it has been taken, HE MUST HAVE BEEN ACCOMPANIED BY AN AIRWAY-CAPABLE DOCTOR, and the plan is unchanged.' THE STRIDOR GOING QUIET WITH DROWSINESS: 'QUIETENING STRIDOR WITH DROWSINESS IS IMPENDING COMPLETE OBSTRUCTION, NOT IMPROVEMENT. I'm calling the arrest team, THE MOST SENIOR AIRWAY OPERATOR INTUBATES NOW — GAS INDUCTION, UPRIGHT — WITH A SURGICAL AIRWAY KIT OPEN AT THE BEDSIDE. Two-person bag-mask with jaw thrust until then.' VERIFY A SORE-THROAT DOOR: same station, explore the sore throat first, and the red flags land in the same place. A FULLY IMMUNISED CHILD: 'IMMUNISATION MAKES Hib UNLIKELY BUT DOES NOT EXCLUDE EPIGLOTTITIS — PNEUMOCOCCUS, GROUP A STREP AND STAPH CAUSE IT IN VACCINATED CHILDREN. THE CLINICAL PICTURE DECIDES; THE MANAGEMENT IS THE SAME.'
plan: VITALS, THEN THE FEAR ACKNOWLEDGED WITHOUT TOUCHING THE CHILD: 'Examiner, may I have his observations first?' → 39.6, HR 150, SpO2 94%. Then, at her level: 'I can see he's working hard AND I CAN SEE YOU'RE FRIGHTENED. HE'S IN THE RIGHT PLACE and the nurses are with him. Tell me what's happened.' → 'he was fine at lunch. About three hours ago he started sounding funny and HE WON'T LIE DOWN. IS HE GOING TO STOP BREATHING?' → 'WE ARE GOING TO LOOK AFTER HIS BREATHING — THAT'S MY WHOLE FOCUS.'

THE COMPLAINT AND THE DISCRIMINATOR: 'IS IT MAINLY A NOISE, OR IS HE STRUGGLING FOR BREATH? What does the noise sound like — A HARSH SOUND WHEN HE BREATHES IN, OR A RATTLE? Is it getting worse? Anything better or worse — LYING DOWN, MOVING ABOUT? HAS HE BEEN COUGHING AT ALL?' → 'NO, HE HASN'T COUGHED AT ALL.' → SAY IT: 'NO COUGH — THAT'S IMPORTANT.'

FEVER AND ENT, THEN THE THREE RED FLAGS ASKED TOGETHER: 'has he had a fever — did you measure it, any chills, did you give anything? Sore throat? Ear pain? Runny nose? NOW THREE IMPORTANT ONES: IS HE DROOLING OR DRIBBLING? HAS HIS VOICE CHANGED — MUFFLED, LIKE SOMETHING HOT IN HIS MOUTH? IS HE REFUSING TO SWALLOW — SPITTING OUT SALIVA? Any lumps in the neck? Any rash? HOW IS HE SITTING?' (Once you have drooling, STOP AND ASK THE OTHER RED FLAGS TOGETHER — drifting back to 'any vomiting?' before finishing them reads as not recognising the emergency.)

THE QUICK SCREENS AND THE HIDDEN CLUE: wheeze, night cough, puffers; A CHOKING EPISODE WHILE EATING OR PLAYING; coughing fits or vomiting after coughing; grunting; tummy symptoms; IS HE HIS NORMAL SELF OR FLOPPY AND SLEEPY, DRINKING, LAST WEE. Then: 'ARE HIS IMMUNISATIONS UP TO DATE?' → she looks down: 'HE HAD THE SIX-MONTH ONES. THEN WE MOVED AND IT DIDN'T HAPPEN.' → NOTE IT ALOUD: 'SO THE TWELVE- AND EIGHTEEN-MONTH ONES WERE MISSED. THAT'S USEFUL TO KNOW.' Then medical problems, medicines, allergies, sick contacts.

THE EXAMINATION — GENERAL APPEARANCE FIRST, THEN THE REFUSAL: 'general appearance: is he ALERT OR DROWSY? Does he look TOXIC? Dehydration? IS HE DROOLING? WHAT POSITION IS HE IN? IS THERE AUDIBLE STRIDOR? Any RECESSION, TRACHEAL TUG OR CYANOSIS?' Then: 'saturations 94% on room air. I AM NOT GOING TO EXAMINE HIS THROAT, EARS OR NOSE — I'M CONCERNED ABOUT EPIGLOTTITIS AND I DON'T WANT TO PRECIPITATE OBSTRUCTION. Chest, WITH MINIMAL HANDLING: air entry, added sounds? Heart sounds? I'll defer the abdomen and neck.' → THE EXAMINER TESTS YOU: 'WOULD YOU LIKE TO LOOK AT HIS THROAT?' → 'NO. In a drooling, toxic child with stridor, THE THROAT IS EXAMINED BY THE AIRWAY TEAM IN A CONTROLLED SETTING.'

THE DIAGNOSIS IN SHORT SENTENCES WITH FIVE REASONS, THEN THE DIFFERENTIALS (see dx) → 'IS IT BECAUSE WE MISSED HIS NEEDLES? IS THIS MY FAULT?' / 'ISN'T IT JUST CROUP?' → 'THIS ISN'T ABOUT BLAME — IT'S ABOUT GETTING HIM SAFE.' (If you blame her she becomes defensive and stops answering freely.)

MANAGEMENT IN ORDER — UPRIGHT AND UNDISTURBED, OXYGEN, THE AIRWAY TEAM AND MedSTAR, THEN ANTIBIOTICS ONCE THE AIRWAY IS SAFE (see dx). (Leading with 'IV antibiotics' and forgetting the airway team has missed the point.)

Then to the examiner: 'an UNDER-IMMUNISED 4-year-old with ACUTE EPIGLOTTITIS AND IMPENDING AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION. Upright, minimal handling, oxygen, airway team and MedSTAR Kids, nil by mouth, IV CEFTRIAXONE ONCE THE AIRWAY PLAN IS MADE, PICU, notification and contact prophylaxis. QUIETENING STRIDOR OR DROWSINESS MEANS IMMEDIATE INTUBATION.'

pefe: Role-player: EMMA, 29, a hairdresser in Kadina, SOLE PARENT of Oliver (4) and MIA (18 months). Oliver was WELL AT LUNCH; over THREE HOURS he became feverish, started DRIBBLING, SOUNDS MUFFLED, REFUSES TO SWALLOW and makes A HARSH NOISE BREATHING IN. HE WILL NOT LIE DOWN AND SITS LEANING FORWARD. NO COUGH. You gave paracetamol WITH NO EFFECT. He is on your lap throughout — THE CHILD IS NOT PLAYED.

IMMUNISATIONS: he had the 2-, 4- AND 6-MONTH VACCINES; THEN YOU MOVED TOWNS AFTER A RELATIONSHIP BREAKDOWN AND THE 12- AND 18-MONTH ONES NEVER HAPPENED. YOU ARE ASHAMED OF THIS AND WILL ONLY VOLUNTEER IT IF ASKED DIRECTLY. IF THE DOCTOR BLAMES YOU, BECOME DEFENSIVE AND STOP ANSWERING FREELY; IF THE DOCTOR SAYS IT IS NOT ABOUT BLAME, SOFTEN. HIDDEN AGENDA: 'IS HE GOING TO STOP BREATHING?' asked early; 'CAN'T YOU JUST LOOK IN HIS THROAT, OR GIVE HIM SOMETHING?' pushed once after the doctor declines; and 'CAN I STAY WITH HIM? WHAT ABOUT MIA?' at the end. REGISTER: frightened, fast-talking, TEARFUL AT THE VACCINE QUESTION.

EXAMINER CARD — ONLY GIVE A FINDING IF ASKED FOR BY NAME. Obs: T 39.6, HR 150, RR 36, SpO2 94% RA, CRT 2 s. General: IRRITABLE, TOXIC, DRY LIPS, DROOLING, TRIPOD, SOFT STRIDOR AT REST, MILD SUPRASTERNAL RECESSION, NO CYANOSIS. back.dx: FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOW, CULTURES, AND IV ANTIBIOTIC WITHIN 60 MINUTES, WHATEVER THE CARD SHOWS. EXPLAIN IT IN CONTEXT: 'Liam looks well, and I can see why you might wonder IF THIS IS JUST A COLD FROM HIS SISTER. But my main concern is a situation we call FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA. Liam has leukaemia, which is A CANCER OF THE WHITE BLOOD CELLS, and last week's chemotherapy PUSHES THE NUMBER OF INFECTION-FIGHTING WHITE CELLS — THE NEUTROPHILS — RIGHT DOWN; EIGHT DAYS AFTER A CYCLE IS WHEN THEY'RE LOWEST. So right now HIS BODY HAS VERY LITTLE TO FIGHT AN INFECTION WITH, AND IT ALSO CAN'T SHOW US HOW BAD AN INFECTION IS — IT CAN'T MAKE THE PUS AND SWELLING THAT USUALLY TELL US. That means A FEVER, EVEN IN A CHILD WHO LOOKS WELL, HAS TO BE TREATED AS A POSSIBLY SERIOUS INFECTION UNTIL THE TESTS PROVE OTHERWISE. The red ear and throat may be where it's started, but I CAN'T RELY ON THEM TO TELL ME IT'S MILD.' AND ANSWER THE RELAPSE QUESTION HONESTLY: 'NOTHING TODAY SUGGESTS THAT — THIS IS ABOUT INFECTION WHILE HIS COUNTS ARE LOW, AND HIS TEAM WILL CHECK HIS BLOOD.' MANAGEMENT: 'Liam needs to go to the EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOW — I'll RING AHEAD AND SPEAK TO HIS ONCOLOGY TEAM so they're expecting him. In hospital THE VERY FIRST THING IS TO TAKE BLOOD FOR CULTURES FROM HIS PORT AND FROM A VEIN, AND THEN, WITHIN THE HOUR AND WITHOUT WAITING FOR ANY RESULTS, GIVE HIM STRONG ANTIBIOTICS STRAIGHT INTO THE VEIN. After that a full examination and A SEPSIS WORK-UP: a full blood count to see how low his white cells are, inflammatory markers, urine, and if needed A CHEST X-RAY, A NOSE AND THROAT SWAB, OR A LUMBAR PUNCTURE. PARACETAMOL FOR THE FEVER — NOT IBUPROFEN, BECAUSE HIS PLATELETS MAY BE LOW. He'll be admitted under his oncology team, who will decide about transfer, and they'll REVIEW HIM AT 48 HOURS with the results. PATS can help with travel and accommodation, and I'll give you a letter.' REFUSE THE TWO REQUESTS: 'CAN'T YOU JUST GIVE HIM ANTIBIOTICS HERE AND WE GO HOME?' → 'I understand the appeal, BUT TABLETS AREN'T ENOUGH HERE — he needs them INTO A VEIN, IN HOSPITAL, WITH BLOOD TESTS TAKEN FIRST, AND SOMEONE WATCHING HIM OVERNIGHT. If he were to get sicker, THAT CAN HAPPEN QUICKLY WITH LOW WHITE CELLS.' AND IF THE EXAMINER ASKS 'ISN'T IT BETTER TO CHECK THE NEUTROPHIL COUNT AND THEN DECIDE?' → 'NO — I ASSUME HE'S NEUTROPENIC; THE COUNT CONFIRMS IT BUT DOESN'T CHANGE THE FIRST HOUR.' (The role-player is briefed to look relieved if you say check the bloods first, AND LET YOU FAIL.) VERSION B — THE SHOCKED CHILD: 'he's DROWSY WITH A FOUR-SECOND CAPILLARY REFILL AND A HEART RATE OF 150 — THIS IS SEPTIC SHOCK. I'm calling MedSTAR and the emergency department now, getting IV OR INTRAOSSEOUS ACCESS, giving OXYGEN AND A 20 mL/kg BOLUS, and, if we stock it, IV CEFTRIAXONE AFTER CULTURES on oncology advice.' VERIFY THE ADULT EQUIVALENT, WORTH KNOWING: an adult ON CARBIMAZOLE with a sore throat and fever — 'SAME RULE: STOP THE CARBIMAZOLE, URGENT FULL BLOOD COUNT TODAY, AND IF THE NEUTROPHILS ARE LOW HE GOES TO ED FOR IV ANTIBIOTICS.'

Then: 'I CAN SEE HE'S BEING TREATED FOR LEUKAEMIA. Tell me what's been happening.' → 'the hospital told us if he ever gets a fever WE HAVE TO GET HIM SEEN STRAIGHT AWAY. He seems okay in himself, but they said not to wait.' → 'YOU DID EXACTLY THE RIGHT THING.'

THE FEVER: 'how high has it been? Since when? All the time or on and off? Have you given anything — AND DOES IT HELP? ANY SHIVERING OR SHAKING, ESPECIALLY AFTER HIS PORT HAS BEEN FLUSHED?' → paracetamol helps for a few hours. (A GOOD PARACETAMOL RESPONSE IS THE REASSURANCE BAIT — IT CHANGES NOTHING.)

THE LEUKAEMIA BLOCK — nine questions: 'WHEN WAS HE DIAGNOSED? WHAT TREATMENT IS HE ON, AND WHICH PHASE? WHEN EXACTLY WAS THE LAST CHEMOTHERAPY? DOES HE HAVE A PORT OR CENTRAL LINE? WERE HIS LAST BLOOD COUNTS LOW? ANY TRANSFUSIONS? IS HE ON PREVENTIVE MEDICINES LIKE CO-TRIMOXAZOLE? ANY STEROIDS THIS CYCLE? WHO IS HIS ONCOLOGY TEAM, AND DID THEY GIVE YOU A FEVER PLAN OR CARD?' → EIGHT DAYS AGO. → SAY IT: 'THAT PUTS HIM RIGHT AT THE POINT HIS WHITE CELLS ARE LOWEST.' And ASK FOR THE FEVER CARD — it usually names the antibiotic and the number to call.

THE SEVEN GROUPS PLUS THE EXTRA SITES: ear pain, runny nose, sore throat, MOUTH ULCERS, drooling, voice change, neck lumps, rash; cough, breathlessness, noisy breathing; vomiting, diarrhoea, tummy pain, PAIN AROUND THE BOTTOM; burning or frequency passing urine; swollen or red joints, limping, red skin, ANY REDNESS AROUND THE PORT; headache, stiff neck, photophobia. → ONLY POSITIVES: A RUNNY NOSE AND A SCRATCHY THROAT. (The examiner is watching whether you RUN THE WHOLE STRUCTURE OR STOP AT 'IT'S A COLD'.)

WELL-CHILD AND CIST: alert or drowsy, eating and drinking, passing urine as usual; travel; anyone unwell at home or school; AND 'IMMUNISATIONS — AND WHICH ARE ON HOLD?' → his sister had a cold, and NO LIVE VACCINES DURING TREATMENT.

THE EXAMINATION CARD WITH THE NEUTROPENIA SWEEP: general appearance INCLUDING BRUISING, PALLOR AND MOUTH ULCERS; vitals with CRT and saturations; ENT including the mouth; chest; heart; abdomen with liver and spleen; FULL JOINT EXAMINATION; FULL LYMPH NODE EXAMINATION; neck stiffness; urine dipstick; AND THE PORT SITE — REDNESS, TENDERNESS, DISCHARGE — THE SKIN AND NAIL FOLDS — AND THE PERIANAL AREA ON INSPECTION ONLY.
THE SENTENCE THAT IS THE MARK, SAID AFTER THE CARD: 'A POSSIBLE UPPER RESPIRATORY SOURCE, BUT IN A NEUTROPENIC CHILD A MILD-LOOKING EAR DOES NOT MEAN A MILD INFECTION.'
THE DIAGNOSIS IN CONTEXT, WITH THE MECHANISM IN PLAIN WORDS (see dx) → 'BUT HE'S PLAYING — HE DOESN'T SEEM SICK AT ALL.' / 'IS THE LEUKAEMIA BACK?' → answer it honestly.

Then summarise.

pefe: Role-player: SARAH, 34, Liam's mother. LIAM IS 6, diagnosed with ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKAEMIA FOUR MONTHS AGO at the Women's and Children's; now in CONSOLIDATION; LAST CHEMOTHERAPY EIGHT DAYS AGO; HAS A PORT. Takes BACTRIM ON WEEKENDS. No steroids this cycle. No recent transfusions. You live in Wallaroo; Dad works FIFO and is away. LIAM'S SISTER, 9, HAD A COLD LAST WEEK. YOU HAVE THE HOSPITAL'S FEVER CARD IN YOUR BAG WITH THE ONCOLOGY NUMBER, BUT YOU ONLY MENTION IT IF ASKED ABOUT A PLAN OR WHO TO CALL.

REGISTER: calm, organised, SLIGHTLY EMBARRASSED — YOU FEEL YOU MAY BE OVER-REACTING BECAUSE HE LOOKS FINE. You become anxious only if the doctor uses the word 'sepsis' or 'serious' WITHOUT EXPLAINING. HIDDEN AGENDA: YOU ARE AFRAID THE LEUKAEMIA HAS COME BACK — ask 'IS IT BACK?' when the diagnosis is explained, or volunteer it near the end if the doctor never asks about your worries. PUSH: IF THE DOCTOR RECOMMENDS HOSPITAL, ASK WHETHER ANTIBIOTICS COULD BE GIVEN HERE AND YOU GO HOME; IF THEY SAY TO CHECK THE BLOODS FIRST, LOOK RELIEVED — AND LET THEM FAIL.

HONESTLY; ED NOW WITH CULTURES THEN IV ANTIBIOTICS WITHIN THE HOUR, BEFORE RESULTS; named the sepsis work-up and PARACETAMOL NOT IBUPROFEN; oncology team contacted and PATS; REFUSED ORAL ANTIBIOTICS AT HOME; and summarised.

back.dx: SEPTIC ARTHRITIS OF THE KNEE — HOSPITAL TODAY, CULTURES BEFORE ANTIBIOTICS. VERSION A: 'Tom most likely has a condition called SEPTIC ARTHRITIS IN HIS RIGHT KNEE. Put simply, THAT IS AN INFECTION INSIDE THE JOINT. The reasons I think this are THE FEVER, WHICH TELLS ME THERE IS AN INFECTION; THE SWELLING YOU NOTICED; and when I examined the knee IT WAS RED, WARM AND PAINFUL TO TOUCH, AND HE WON'T PUT WEIGHT ON IT.' VERSION B: '...most likely has OSTEOMYELITIS — AN INFECTION IN THE BONE JUST BELOW THE KNEE. The reasons are the fever, the swelling and redness, and that WHEN I EXAMINED HIM THE MOST PAINFUL SPOT WAS ON THE BONE RATHER THAN THE JOINT ITSELF. THE INFECTION CAN SPREAD INTO THE JOINT, SO SEPTIC ARTHRITIS IS MY SECOND CONCERN.' THE DIFFERENTIALS, WITH OSTEOMYELITIS AND CELLULITIS NAMED BEFORE THE GROUP LIST: 'AN INFECTION IN THE BONE NEXT TO THE JOINT, CALLED OSTEOMYELITIS; AN INFECTION IN THE SKIN OVER THE KNEE, CALLED CELLULITIS; AN IRRITABLE JOINT AFTER A COLD, WHICH IS USUALLY MILDER THAN THIS; AND AN INJURY. I have also checked for the usual infections of the ears, throat, chest, tummy and urine, AND FOR MENINGITIS, and I didn't find any.' NEVER GIVE ORGANISMS — NOT STAPH, NOT KINGELLA — AS DIFFERENTIALS. HIS QUESTIONS: 'HOW DID HE GET THAT?' → 'usually BACTERIA FROM A SMALL SKIN BREAK OR FROM THE BLOODSTREAM SETTLE IN THE JOINT; IT ISN'T ANYONE'S FAULT.' 'CAN'T YOU JUST GIVE HIM ANTIBIOTICS?' → 'ANTIBIOTICS ARE ESSENTIAL, BUT THEY NEED TO GO INTO A VEIN IN HOSPITAL, AND THE JOINT USUALLY NEEDS TO BE WASHED OUT SO THE INFECTION DOESN'T DAMAGE THE CARTILAGE.' 'WILL HE WALK PROPERLY?' → 'TREATED QUICKLY, MOST CHILDREN WALK NORMALLY AFTERWARDS — WHICH IS WHY WE ACT TODAY.' AND THE COUCH FALL: 'THAT MAY WELL BE PART OF IT, AND I'LL ASK THE HOSPITAL TO X-RAY THE LEG. BUT A HOT, SWOLLEN JOINT WITH A FEVER OF 39 HAS TO BE TREATED AS AN INFECTION UNTIL THE TESTS PROVE OTHERWISE — WAITING WOULD RISK THE JOINT.' MANAGEMENT IF ASKED: 'Tom needs to go to the Women's and Children's Hospital TODAY. I'll RING THE ORTHOPAEDIC AND PAEDIATRIC TEAMS NOW and arrange the ambulance. PLEASE DON'T GIVE HIM ANYTHING TO EAT OR DRINK FROM NOW, IN CASE HE NEEDS A SHORT ANAESTHETIC TO TAKE FLUID FROM THE KNEE. In hospital they will take BLOOD TESTS AND BLOOD CULTURES FIRST, do AN ULTRASOUND, and then START ANTIBIOTICS THROUGH A DRIP AND WASH OUT THE JOINT.' PATS for travel, and practice follow-up. NO ORAL ANTIBIOTICS FROM THE SURGERY. THE VARIANTS: A FREELY MOBILE JOINT IN A CHILD WHO HAS JUST WALKED ACROSS THE ROOM — 'A FREELY MOBILE JOINT WITH SPREADING SKIN REDNESS MAKES CELLULITIS MORE LIKELY THAN SEPTIC ARTHRITIS. I'd still CHECK INFLAMMATORY MARKERS TODAY AND ARRANGE REVIEW WITHIN 24 HOURS, and I would refer IF HE STOPS WEIGHT-BEARING OR THE FEVER PERSISTS.' THE WELL-BABY ANSWERS TURNING BAD — FLOPPY, MOTTLED, CRT 4 SECONDS: 'THIS IS NOW SEPSIS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE. I'm calling MedSTAR for retrieval, GAINING IV ACCESS, TAKING CULTURES AND GIVING THE FIRST DOSE OF IV ANTIBIOTICS HERE BEFORE TRANSFER.'
plan: VITALS, THEN ACKNOWLEDGE: 'Examiner, the vital signs please?' → 39.0, HR 150, CRT 2 s. → 'he is FEBRILE AND HIS HEART RATE IS UP, BUT HE IS PERFUSING WELL.' Then: 'tell me what's been happening.' → fever since yesterday, grizzly, off his food. → 'A FEVER OF 39 IN A ONE-YEAR-OLD IS WORRYING, I UNDERSTAND.'

THE FEVER: measured, since when, constant or on and off, getting worse, what have you given and does it help, ANY SHIVERING. → paracetamol helps for a few hours, AND HE SHIVERED LAST NIGHT. (A helpful antipyretic response IS THE NORMAL PATTERN AND DOES NOT MAKE THE CHILD SAFE.)

THE SOURCE HUNT, GROUPS ONE TO FOUR: ears and throat — pulling at his ears, runny nose, DROOLING, CHANGE IN HIS CRY, neck lumps, rash; chest — cough, difficulty breathing, noisy breathing; tummy — vomiting, diarrhoea, DRAWING HIS LEGS UP; nappies — smelly wee, crying at changes. → all negative, BUT: 'HE DOES SCREAM WHENEVER I PICK HIM UP, THOUGH. I THOUGHT HE WAS JUST BEING GRUMPY.'

FOLLOW THE BRIDGE IMMEDIATELY — THIS IS THE STATION: 'that's important, thank you. WHEN YOU PICK HIM UP, DOES ANY PART OF HIM SEEM SORE? HAVE YOU NOTICED ANY SWOLLEN OR RED JOINTS? IS HE STANDING AND CRAWLING THE WAY HE NORMALLY DOES?' → THE RIGHT KNEE IS PUFFY AND PINK. Then explore it fully: 'WHICH KNEE? SINCE WHEN? RED? HOT? DOES HE LET YOU TOUCH IT? ANY FALL OR BUMP? WHO'S BEEN LOOKING AFTER HIM? ANY OTHER JOINT? ANY RASH NEAR IT?'

MENINGITIS, WELL-BABY AND CIST: headache signs are hard at this age, so ask about DROWSY OR FLOPPY, feeding and drinking, WET NAPPIES; then travel, anyone unwell at home or daycare, AND IMMUNISATIONS INCLUDING THE 12-MONTH ONES.

THE EXAMINATION — GENERAL FIRST, THEN INSPECT, PALPATE, LOCATE: 'general appearance: alert or drowsy? Dehydration? Rash? IS HE HOLDING A LEG STILL? Vitals. ENT. Chest. Heart. Abdomen. NECK STIFFNESS. DIPSTICK. Lymph nodes. NOW THE JOINTS: ON INSPECTION, IS ANY JOINT SWOLLEN OR RED, AND WHICH? ON PALPATION, IS IT WARM TO TOUCH AND TENDER TO TOUCH? WHERE IS THE TENDERNESS — ACROSS THE JOINT LINE OR OVER THE TIBIAL TUBEROSITY? EFFUSION? OTHER JOINTS AND THE HIP ON THAT SIDE?' (Asking to MOVE the knee wastes twenty seconds; NOT asking WHERE it is tender loses Version B.)
THE DIAGNOSIS WITH ITS REASONS, THEN OSTEOMYELITIS AND CELLULITIS BEFORE THE GROUP LIST (see dx) → 'AN INFECTION IN THE JOINT? HOW DID HE GET THAT?' / 'CAN'T YOU JUST GIVE HIM ANTIBIOTICS?'

THE COUCH FALL REFUSED AS THE EXPLANATION, AND MANAGEMENT IF ASKED (see dx): hospital today, ring the orthopaedic team, NIL BY MOUTH FOR A POSSIBLE ANAESTHETIC, cultures and ultrasound before IV antibiotics and washout, PATS. → 'MY WIFE IS AT WORK — CAN I RING HER?' → yes, while you make the calls. Then summarise to the examiner.

pefe: Role-player: MARK, 34, Tom's father, A DIESEL MECHANIC IN KADINA; his wife is a nurse on shift and TOLD HIM TO BRING TOM IN. TOM IS 13 MONTHS, born at term, FULLY IMMUNISED INCLUDING THE 12-MONTH VACCINES, at daycare two days a week. He has felt hot since yesterday — 39 ON THE FOREHEAD THERMOMETER ONCE, otherwise not measured. Paracetamol helps for a few hours. HE SHIVERED LAST NIGHT. He is grizzly, HARDLY DRINKING, THREE WET NAPPIES TODAY, awake but miserable. HIS RIGHT KNEE LOOKED PUFFY AND PINK THIS MORNING AND FEELS WARM; HE CRIES IF YOU TOUCH IT; HE WILL NOT STAND OR CRAWL. No fall that you know of. Runny nose last week, gone.

HIDDEN AGENDA: YOU FEEL GUILTY THAT YOU DID NOT NOTICE THE KNEE EARLIER AND WORRY YOUR WIFE WILL BLAME YOU. REGISTER: practical, a bit embarrassed, BECOMES ANXIOUS WHEN HOSPITAL IS MENTIONED. HOW TO PLAY IT: VOLUNTEER ONLY THE FEVER AND THE GRIZZLINESS. SAY 'HE SCREAMS WHENEVER I PICK HIM UP' ONCE, UNPROMPTED, AFTER THE TUMMY OR NAPPY QUESTIONS — THEN WAIT. MENTION THE KNEE ONLY IF ASKED ABOUT JOINTS, SORENESS, STANDING OR CRAWLING. IF THE DOCTOR SUGGESTS ANTIBIOTIC SYRUP AND REVIEW TOMORROW, ASK 'IS THAT ENOUGH?' IF ASKED ABOUT A FALL, SAY 'HE FELL OFF THE COUCH LAST WEEK, BUT HE WAS FINE AFTER' AND SEE WHETHER THE DOCTOR DROPS THE INFECTION IDEA. If not asked about worries by minute six, say 'IS IT SOMETHING I DID?'

Score them on: ASKED VITALS FIRST; acknowledged your worry; explored the fever — measured, medication, whether it helps; NAMED THE GROUPS — ENT, chest, tummy, nappies, JOINTS AND SKIN, meningitis, sepsis; RESPONDED TO 'SCREAMS WHEN PICKED UP' WITH JOINT AND SORENESS QUESTIONS; EXPLORED THE KNEE — which, since when, red, warm, touch, standing, other joints, rash, FALL, CARERS; the well-baby questions; travel, contacts and immunisation; THE EXAMINATION AS INSPECT, PALPATE, THEN WHERE TENDER — DID NOT ASK TO MOVE IT — AND ASKED ABOUT THE HIP; SAID 'SEPTIC ARTHRITIS — INFECTION INSIDE THE JOINT' WITH REASONS; DIFFERENTIALS OSTEOMYELITIS AND CELLULITIS THEN THE GROUPS; HOSPITAL TODAY, NO ORAL ANTIBIOTICS, NIL BY MOUTH; DID NOT ACCEPT THE COUCH FALL AS THE EXPLANATION; and summarised to the examiner.
fails: ★ Not following 'he screams whenever I pick him up' with joint and soreness questions — the father says it once and then waits, and the knee never appears unless you ask
★ Not asking where the tenderness is — across the joint line or over the tibial tuberosity — which makes Version B a wrong diagnosis
Accepting the couch fall as the explanation and dropping the infection idea
Offering oral antibiotics and review tomorrow, when he asks 'is that enough?' and the answer is hospital today

Asking to move the knee, which wastes twenty seconds; forgetting to ask about the hip on that side; and giving organisms such as Staph or Kingella as differentials instead of osteomyelitis and cellulitis

stem: General practice. LIAM, 5 YEARS, brought in by his mother SARAH with FEVER FOR TWO DAYS. HER STATED CONCERN: SHE IS WORRIED HE HAS MENINGOCOCCAEMIA — A CHILD AT A NEARBY SCHOOL WAS RECENTLY ADMITTED WITH IT.

Initial information: T 38.4 at home this morning, PARACETAMOL HELPS FOR A FEW HOURS THEN THE FEVER RETURNS. HE IS DRINKING, PASSING URINE AND PLAYING BETWEEN FEVERS. History 4 minutes, examination findings from the examiner, explain the diagnosis AND ADDRESS HER CONCERN ABOUT MENINGOCOCCAEMIA, then explain your management. back.dx: SCARLET FEVER — GROUP A STREPTOCOCCAL PHARYNGITIS WITH THE TOXIN RASH. NAME IT AND EXPLAIN IT: 'I'm confident Liam has an infection called SCARLET FEVER. IT'S A THROAT INFECTION CAUSED BY A COMMON BACTERIUM CALLED STREPTOCOCCUS — the same one that causes strep throat — AND IN SOME CHILDREN THE BUG MAKES A TOXIN THAT PRODUCES THIS PARTICULAR RASH.' FIVE REASONS: 'THE SORE THROAT AND FEVER, HIS TONSILS INFLAMED WITH WHITE PATCHES, THE RASH ROUGH LIKE SANDPAPER THAT FADES WHEN PRESSED, THE PALE RING AROUND HIS MOUTH, AND THE RED BUMPY STRAWBERRY LOOK OF HIS TONGUE.' Say BOTH names if you like — 'scarlet fever, a strep throat infection with its rash' — BUT THE MARKING SCHEME SAYS SCARLET FEVER. THEN THE CONCERN, ANSWERED WITH THREE REASONS RATHER THAN REASSURANCE: 'I DON'T THINK THIS IS MENINGOCOCCAL DISEASE, FOR THREE REASONS. CHILDREN WITH MENINGOCOCCAL ARE VERY UNWELL AND DROWSY — LIAM IS ALERT AND PLAYING. THEIR RASH IS DARK AND DOESN'T FADE UNDER PRESSURE — LIAM'S FADES AND IS ROUGH, WHICH IS THE STREP PATTERN. AND HIS HEART RATE, BREATHING AND CIRCULATION SHOW NO SIGN OF A BODY-WIDE INFECTION. NOTHING IN MEDICINE IS ONE HUNDRED PER CENT, SO I'LL GIVE YOU EXACTLY WHAT TO WATCH FOR.' MANAGEMENT: CHECK THE ALLERGY FIRST — 'does Liam have any allergies, PARTICULARLY TO PENICILLIN?' Then: 'BECAUSE THE STREP BUG IS ALREADY SHOWING ON HIS SKIN, THIS IS ONE THROAT INFECTION WE DO TREAT WITH ANTIBIOTICS — to clear it and, importantly, TO PROTECT HIS HEART AND KIDNEYS FROM THE RARE COMPLICATIONS OF STREP. PHENOXYMETHYLPENICILLIN SYRUP, TWICE A DAY, FOR TEN FULL DAYS. He'll feel better in two or three days — PLEASE KEEP GOING TO THE END OF THE BOTTLE; THE LENGTH OF THE COURSE IS WHAT DOES THE PROTECTING.' THE SWAB QUESTION: 'A SWAB TAKES A FEW DAYS TO COME BACK AND WOULDN'T CHANGE WHAT WE DO — THE PICTURE IS CLEAR ENOUGH TO TREAT TODAY.' THEN COMFORT, FLUIDS AND EXCLUSION: paracetamol or ibuprofen with food; SMALL DRINKS OFTEN, ICY POLES, SOFT FOOD; AND HOME FROM SCHOOL UNTIL 24 HOURS AFTER THE FIRST DOSE AND HE FEELS WELL. THE SAFETY-NET HAS TWO HALVES, AND THE LATE HALF IS WHAT THE EXAMINER IS LISTENING FOR: TONIGHT — DROWSY OR HARD TO WAKE, NEW SPOTS THAT DON'T FADE UNDER A GLASS, STOPS DRINKING OR PASSING URINE, DROOLING OR NOISY BREATHING; AND IN THE NEXT FEW WEEKS — DARK OR COLA-COLOURED URINE, PUFFY EYES, PAINFUL SWOLLEN JOINTS, CHEST PAIN OR BREATHLESSNESS. Review in two to three days, a fact sheet, AND TEACH-BACK: 'WHAT WILL YOU DO IF HE SEEMS WORSE TONIGHT?' THE VARIANTS: THE TOXIC CHILD — 'this child is DROWSY WITH A NON-BLANCHING RASH AND DELAYED CAPILLARY REFILL. I AM TREATING THIS AS MENINGOCOCCAL SEPTICAEMIA. I'm calling for help, giving HIGH-FLOW OXYGEN, obtaining IV OR INTRAOSSEOUS ACCESS for a 20 mL/kg BOLUS, giving CEFTRIAXONE 50 mg/kg INTRAMUSCULARLY IF ACCESS IS DELAYED, and calling MedSTAR Kids for retrieval. I WILL NOTIFY SA HEALTH.' VERIFY A DECLARED PENICILLIN ALLERGY — 'WHAT HAPPENED WHEN HE HAD PENICILLIN? A rash a few days in, no swelling or breathing trouble — THAT'S A NON-SEVERE REACTION, so I'll use CEFALEXIN TWICE DAILY FOR TEN DAYS. IF IT HAD BEEN SWELLING OR BREATHING DIFFICULTY I WOULD USE AZITHROMYCIN ONCE DAILY FOR FIVE DAYS.' VERIFY AN ABORIGINAL CHILD AT HIGH RHEUMATIC FEVER RISK — 'children in your community have A HIGHER CHANCE OF A STREP THROAT GOING ON TO AFFECT THE HEART — RHEUMATIC FEVER — so this one we definitely treat, and finishing the course matters even more. IF THE TWICE-DAILY SYRUP FOR TEN DAYS WILL BE HARD, A SINGLE INJECTION OF LONG-ACTING PENICILLIN TODAY DOES THE SAME JOB. Would it help if I LINKED IN WITH THE ABORIGINAL HEALTH SERVICE for the follow-up? The medicine is covered under CLOSING THE GAP.'
plan: VITALS, THEN ACKNOWLEDGE THE FEAR IN THE FIRST MINUTE: 'Examiner, may I have Liam's observations?' Then: 'tell me what's been happening.' → 'he's had fevers for two days and I READ ABOUT THAT BOY WITH MENINGOCOCCAL — I JUST WANT TO KNOW IT ISN'T THAT.' → 'THAT'S A FRIGHTENING THING TO HAVE HEARD, AND YOU'VE DONE THE RIGHT THING BRINGING HIM IN. I'll ask some questions, examine him, AND THEN I'LL ANSWER THAT WORRY DIRECTLY.' (If you have not acknowledged it within the first minute, SHE INTERRUPTS WITH 'BUT IS IT MENINGOCOCCAL?')
THE FEVER: measured, highest, what have you given and how much, DOES IT HELP, when it started, constant or on and off, any shivering.

ENT AND THE FIVE RED FLAGS: 'any ear pain or pulling at his ears? Runny nose? SORE THROAT? IS HE DROOLING? HAS HIS VOICE CHANGED? ANY TROUBLE SWALLOWING? NOISY BREATHING? LUMPS IN THE NECK?' → the throat really hurts, and a small lump under the jaw.

THE RASH — AND TWO OF THESE QUESTIONS ARE THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS: 'has he got any rash anywhere? Where did it start and where is it now? Spreading? What colour? Itchy? Painful? Warm? Any weeping? WHEN YOU RUN YOUR HAND OVER IT, IS IT SMOOTH OR ROUGH? ANYTHING ABOUT HIS FACE OR TONGUE? DOES IT FADE IF YOU PRESS A GLASS ON IT?' → 'ROUGH, LIKE FINE SANDPAPER' and 'HIS CHEEKS ARE RED BUT HE LOOKS PALE AROUND HIS MOUTH.' (SHE WILL NOT SAY 'SANDPAPER' UNLESS YOU ASK THE SURFACE, AND WILL NOT MENTION THE MOUTH UNLESS YOU ASK ABOUT THE FACE — ASK BOTH.)

CLUSTERS, SEPSIS SCREEN AND BACKGROUND: cough or fast breathing; vomiting, diarrhoea, tummy pain; pain passing urine; sore or swollen joints, limping; HEADACHE, STIFF NECK, BOTHERED BY LIGHT; IS HE ALERT AND PLAYING BETWEEN FEVERS, DRINKING, PASSING URINE; ANY RED EYES, CRACKED LIPS, SWOLLEN HANDS; immunisations, travel, ANYONE UNWELL AT SCHOOL, past illnesses, medicines, ALLERGIES.

THE EXAMINATION — THE FOUR SIGNS BY NAME, THEN MOVE: 'general appearance — alert or drowsy, dehydration, toxic? IS THERE A RASH — where, what morphology, warm or painful, BLANCHING OR NON-BLANCHING, AND WHAT IS THE SURFACE LIKE? Vital signs? Ears? Nose? Throat — TONSILS SWOLLEN, RED, EXUDATE? IS THERE A STRAWBERRY TONGUE? PALLOR AROUND THE MOUTH? PALATAL PETECHIAE? CERVICAL NODES — which chain, tender, mobile? NECK STIFFNESS? Chest, heart, abdomen, joints, AND ANY PEELING OF HANDS OR FEET?' (Stopping at 'there is a rash', or running a complete systems examination that EATS TASKS 3 AND 4, are the two traps.)

NAME IT WITH FIVE REASONS, THEN ANSWER THE CONCERN WITH THREE REASONS (see dx) → 'SCARLET FEVER? I THOUGHT THAT WAS SOMETHING FROM THE OLDEN DAYS.' → 'IT IS A VERY OLD NAME, BUT IT'S COMMON AND TREATABLE.' (She stays tense if only told 'don't worry', and relaxes visibly once given reasons.)
MANAGEMENT — ALLERGY CHECK FIRST, THEN THE TEN-DAY COURSE WITH ITS REASON, AND THE SWAB DECLINED (see dx) → 'TEN DAYS IS A LOT. CAN'T YOU JUST DO A SWAB TO CHECK IT'S REALLY STREP?'

VARIANT — THE TOXIC CHILD: 'this child is DROWSY WITH A NON-BLANCHING RASH AND DELAYED CAPILLARY REFILL. I AM TREATING THIS AS MENINGOCOCCAL SEPTICAEMIA. I'm calling for help, giving HIGH-FLOW OXYGEN, obtaining IV OR INTRAOSSEOUS ACCESS FOR A 20 mL/kg BOLUS, giving CEFTRIAXONE 50 mg/kg INTRAMUSCULARLY IF ACCESS IS DELAYED, and calling MedSTAR Kids on 1300 13 12 33 for retrieval. I WILL NOTIFY SA HEALTH.' VERIFY / VARIANT — PENICILLIN ALLERGY DECLARED: 'WHAT HAPPENED WHEN HE HAD PENICILLIN? A rash a few days in, no swelling or breathing trouble — THAT'S A NON-SEVERE REACTION, so CEFALEXIN TWICE DAILY FOR TEN DAYS. IF IT HAD BEEN SWELLING OR BREATHING DIFFICULTY I WOULD USE AZITHROMYCIN ONCE DAILY FOR FIVE DAYS.' VERIFY

VARIANT — AN ABORIGINAL CHILD AT HIGH RHEUMATIC FEVER RISK: 'because of where your family is from, children in your community have A HIGHER CHANCE OF A STREP THROAT GOING ON TO AFFECT THE HEART — RHEUMATIC FEVER — so this one we definitely treat, and FINISHING THE COURSE MATTERS EVEN MORE. IF THE TWICE-DAILY SYRUP FOR TEN DAYS WILL BE HARD, A SINGLE INJECTION OF LONG-ACTING PENICILLIN TODAY DOES THE SAME JOB. Would it help if I LINKED IN WITH THE ABORIGINAL HEALTH SERVICE for the follow-up? The medicine is COVERED UNDER CLOSING THE GAP.'

REGISTER: ANXIOUS AND TALKATIVE at the start; YOU INTERRUPT ONCE WITH 'BUT IS IT MENINGOCOCCAL?' IF THE DOCTOR HAS NOT ACKNOWLEDGED IT WITHIN THE FIRST MINUTE. YOU RELAX VISIBLY ONCE GIVEN REASONS; YOU STAY TENSE IF ONLY TOLD 'DON'T WORRY'. HIDDEN AGENDA: you want A CLEAR YES-OR-NO ON MENINGOCOCCAL WITH REASONS, and you privately believe A SWAB OR BLOOD TEST WOULD SETTLE IT — if the doctor never asks whether you have concerns, RAISE THE SWAB DURING THE MANAGEMENT TASK.

HOW TO PLAY IT: VOLUNTEER ONLY THE FEVER AT FIRST. GIVE THE SORE THROAT ONLY WHEN ASKED ENT QUESTIONS. MENTION THE PALE RING AROUND HIS MOUTH ONLY WHEN ASKED ABOUT THE FACE, AND THE ROUGH TEXTURE ONLY WHEN ASKED ABOUT THE SURFACE. PUSH BACK ONCE ON TEN DAYS OF ANTIBIOTICS. Score them on: vitals requested; CONCERN ACKNOWLEDGED EARLY; fever explored; the ENT cluster; ALL FIVE RED FLAGS; asked about the rash unprompted; ASKED THE SURFACE; ASKED THE FACE AND TONGUE; the other clusters and sepsis screen; immunisation, contacts and allergy; the examination with BLANCHING AND SURFACE, TONGUE, PERIORAL PALLOR, NODES, chest and heart; NAMED SCARLET FEVER WITH REASONS; THREE REASONS IT IS NOT MENINGOCOCCAL; ALLERGY CHECK; PHENOXYMETHYLPENICILLIN FOR TEN DAYS; DECLINED THE SWAB WITH A REASON; fever and fluid advice; EXCLUSION FOR 24 HOURS; RED FLAGS INCLUDING THE LATE COMPLICATIONS; and review with teach-back.
